Since The Merge, the world is a wide and unforgiving place. There are few prospects for those born in its outer wilderness, but one thing is certain: those willing to brave its dangers to deliver goods or messages are always in high demand. In this new era, Traders are not viewed as mere merchants, but paladins who battle through the dangers of the wild to bring vital goods to those in need. It is a noble profession that only the brave and foolish take up. Not content to spend your life tilling soil, you decided to change your fortune. Half a decade of saving and savvy trading has allowed you to purchase a few beasts of burden and wagons, as well as some starting trade goods. Now you and your companions must set out into the world to brave its adventures, uncover its mysteries, and find your fortune as a Trader. With your allies — your long-time mentor, Rudolph, and your childhood friend, Thistle — you set out to conquer the world. [[Legacy Points->Legacy Points]] Scenarios ----------- Difficulty: Easy [[Scenario 1: Finding Family (Intro Scenario)->sc1intro]] {<div class="trk-box">|trk>[<div class="trk-head"><b>This session</b><span class="trk-heroes">Heroes: (if: $heroes is 2)[<b class="trk-on">2</b>](else:)[(link-repeat: "2")[(set: $gold to (max: 0, it + 3 * (2 - $heroes)), $heroes to 2)(rerun: ?trk)]] (if: $heroes is 3)[<b class="trk-on">3</b>](else:)[(link-repeat: "3")[(set: $gold to (max: 0, it + 3 * (3 - $heroes)), $heroes to 3)(rerun: ?trk)]] (if: $heroes is 4)[<b class="trk-on">4</b>](else:)[(link-repeat: "4")[(set: $gold to (max: 0, it + 3 * (4 - $heroes)), $heroes to 4)(rerun: ?trk)]] </span></div><div class="trk-lead">Next map turn is led by <b>player (print: ($turn % $heroes) + 1)</b>.</div>(if: $heroes is 2)[<div class="trk-lead">Two heroes: each starts with a Tier I weapon or armor.</div>]<div class="trk-grid"><div class="trk c-doom"><span class="trk-l">Doom</span><span class="trk-v">$doom(if: $doomLimit > 0)[ / $doomLimit](if: $bossAt > 0 and $bossDone is not true)[ · boss at $bossAt]</span><span class="trk-b">(link-repeat: "−")[(set: $doom to (max: 0, it - 1))(rerun: ?trk)](link-repeat: "+")[(set: $doom to it + 1)(rerun: ?trk)]</span></div></div><div class="trk-note">The app adds Doom for map turns and events. Use − and + for prayers and anything else on the board. <span class="trk-reset">(link: "Start a new run")[(restart:)]</span></div>]</div>} <div class="tag-box">''Party tags''<br>(checkbox: 2bind $supported, "Supported") (checkbox: 2bind $renowned, "Renowned") (checkbox: 2bind $married, "Married") (checkbox: 2bind $scarred, "Scarred")</div> Where are you traveling to? Open Plains (link: 'A star marked with "A"')[(set: $region to "A")(go-to: "Encounter")] [[Sandpost]] [[Hearthhome]] [[Donalyn's Wall]] (link: "Eli's Crossing (event space)")[(set: $region to "Eli's Crossing")(go-to: "Encounter")] Azure Coast (link: 'A star marked with "B"')[(set: $region to "B")(go-to: "Encounter")] [[Port Pearl]] (link: "Verdantmarsh (event space)")[(set: $region to "Verdantmarsh")(go-to: "Encounter")] [[Diver's Key]] Hollowlight Forest (link: 'A star marked with "C"')[(set: $region to "C")(go-to: "Encounter")] [[Sacred Silence]] Deadlands (link: 'A star marked with "D"')[(set: $region to "D")(go-to: "Encounter")] (link: 'A star marked with "E"')[(set: $region to "E")(go-to: "Encounter")] [[Traveler's Rest]] Sea of Sand (link: 'A star marked with "F"')[(set: $region to "F")(go-to: "Encounter")] [[Sunken City]] Dragon's Teeth (link: 'A star marked with "G"')[(set: $region to "G")(go-to: "Encounter")] [[Dragon Clan Karst]] Edge of the World (link: 'A star marked with "H"')[(set: $region to "H")(go-to: "Encounter")] [[Ash'Zel]] The Vale (link: 'A star marked with "I"')[(set: $region to "I")(go-to: "Encounter")] [[The Stone Facade]] Elsewhere (link: 'A star marked with "Z"')[(set: $region to "Z")(go-to: "Encounter")] [[Cloudpost]]//''Sandpost''// <div class="art art-town-sandpost"></div> The exterior of this relatively squat tower is a glittering facade of tens of thousands of crystalline pebbles. Short, hooded figures shuffle in and out of an open entrance near its base. A few of them trail in a line, carting goods from a large network of caves peppering the cliffside. A strange smell assaults your nostrils. Rudolph wrinkles his nose. "Kiplings," he says with a note of disdain. Indeed, now that you're closer, you can make out the sand-colored scales of desert kiplings. (if: $scenario is 1 and $scenarioA is 1)["Rudolph! Thistle!" calls a voice. Towering head and shoulders over the lizardfolk, you see an otherwise stout, bearded man calling out to your party, his face split by a wide grin. You recognize a fellow orphan from Hearthhome. [[Martin? What are you doing here?]]] (else:)["Wonder what kind of scam they're running," Rudolph adds with a knowing sigh. As if on cue, one of the small lizardfolk throws back his hood and waddles up to you. He has a bucket of water in one hand and a rag in the other. "Summer special!" he squeaks. "Caravan wash only 1,000 gold. FREE rat skewer included." A second kipling approaches with a rat on a stick. It is charred black. "What a deal!" exclaims Thistle. [[Return->Main]]] (text-colour:lime)[While in a town, each hero may Rest, Pray and Train once per visit, and Shop and Trade as much as they can pay for. Traveling to a town does not consume your movement for your turn or end your turn unless specifically stated by an event.]//''Hearthhome''// <div class="art art-town-hearthhome"></div> From a distance, Hearthhome merely looks like a smattering of tightly packed hills. It is this anonymity that has kept it safe for generations, as unbeknownst to the outside world, those hills hide a warren of homes and rooms carved into both the hillside and underneath it. Hearthhome is home to mostly humans, but it has its fair share of the displaced and the wanderer among its ranks. Arielle runs the orphanage, where children of all shapes and sizes run free: brambling kids with red, gold, or blue skin, with fire eyes or eyes cerulean like the water of white-sand beaches. Humans, half-elves, Avriel, and even a dwarf. Garrick, the old Avriel sergeant, surveys the sprawling vista seen from the cliffside with a satisfied expression, seemingly content with his new home. Mo, the sylvan gardener, oversees all of the farmlands, where a plethora of crops grow in abundance as a result of many hardworking hands. (if: $scenario is 1 and visits is 1)[It is home and you will miss it, but you know that you must find Marla. Arielle approaches you, gives you a tearful hug, waves goodbye, and wishes you godspeed on your journey. ](text-colour:lime)[While in a town, each hero may Rest, Pray and Train once per visit, and Shop and Trade as much as they can pay for. Traveling to a town does not consume your movement for your turn or end your turn unless specifically stated by an event.] [[Return->Main]]//''Port Pearl''// <div class="art art-town-port-pearl"></div> Never has a city embodied commerce so much as Port Pearl. Men and women of all shapes and sizes, races, creeds, and classes stroll the bustling seaside city, hawking their wares in vigorous shouting matches and attempting to haggle with just about anyone who maintains eye contact for more than a few seconds. There is a certain carefree attitude you notice that is different from the other cities of the world. People dress in baggy clothes and tailored vestments of a hundred different colors. They sport bonny hats and do-rags, and swashbuckle merrily in the streets, play-acting at pirates. Sailors tell tall tales of krakens and mighty beasts, and of the angelic Avriel who watch from on high to rescue overboard men. More than once, you see a few appraising glances cast your way. Traders are competition, after all, or perhaps your profession has a certain allure that draws the eyes of sedentary stall merchants. (if: $scenario is 1 and $dietrichMet is not true)[(set: $dietrichMet to true)Dietrich is found here, although he is not as you remember him. The once-scrawny youth has grown into a man, swarthy and dark-bearded, with a confident swagger and a charming smile. He is flanked by fawning women on both sides, and you notice a cutlass strapped to his belt. He looks at you, and it takes a moment. The slow dawn of recognition lights his face. "You," he says, pointing at you. "Me," you reply. "What are you doing here?" he asks abruptly. "I'm looking for Marla," you say. At the mention of her name, his face darkens. "You won't find her here, and I don't want to say more on the subject." [[Press him.->Port Pearl: Press him]] [[Leave it be.->Port Pearl: Leave it be]]](else:)[(text-colour:lime)[While in a town, each hero may Rest, Pray and Train once per visit, and Shop and Trade as much as they can pay for. Traveling to a town does not consume your movement for your turn or end your turn unless specifically stated by an event.] [[Return->Main]]]//''Diver's Key''// <div class="art art-town-divers-key"></div> The idyllic port town of Diver's Key is maintained by a healthy fishing economy and what you suspect is the equivalent of tourism in this world. Of course, it is dangerous to travel much at all, but you see many older folks lounging on the beach here or resting by the palm trees, at odds with the slightly more rough-and-tumble nature of the sailors and the locals. You don't notice much of a military presence either, which leaves you wondering how the place stays safe at all. "Northmen," says a passerby, answering your unspoken question. "They raid and plunder up and down the coast, but for some reason, Diver's Key is sacred to them. They won't touch it, and anybody that tries to touch it, well, let's just say they don't last very long once the Northmen find out." (if: $palmTreasure is true and $palmDone is not true)[(set: $palmDone to true)(go-to: "Palm: The tavern")](text-colour:lime)[While in a town, each hero may Rest, Pray and Train once per visit, and Shop and Trade as much as they can pay for. Traveling to a town does not consume your movement for your turn or end your turn unless specifically stated by an event.] [[Return->Main]]//''Sacred Silence''// <div class="art art-town-sacred-silence"></div> Sacred Silence is like no other city you've seen before. Intricate, swirling spirals of wooden architecture climb trees that scrape the heavens themselves, with long wooden rope bridges suspended hundreds of feet in the air where men, women, and children walk without concern or care. The entrance, a wreath of berries and tangled vines, creates an arch at which elvish guards stand watch, gesturing with spears in your direction. "We do not prefer foreigners in our fair city," one says to you. "But we will allow you to ply your wares. Be mindful of our rules, and break none of them, lest you be met with swift justice." You cross the threshold and enter a forest-floor square thronged with folk. Almost all of them are elven: fair-skinned, with red, gold, blonde, or brown hair and piercing eyes, willowy and graceful, and fierce in their demeanor. Many of them bear tribal paints and are adorned with feathers, fangs, or other savage accoutrements. They are half-elves, you remind yourself, not full-blooded: those that sought to distance themselves from their immortal, airy parentage by connecting with the forest. The Uktali, they call themselves. Few are friendly-looking, but they take your coin, sure enough. The lack of hawking feels odd to you; when people do talk, it is gently and reverently. Animals roam freely here, and none are burdened with leashes or reins. All kinds are seen: bears, horses, lynxes, and more, all living in harmony. They are seemingly perfectly behaved and completely fastidious. "Truly," remarks Thistle, "this is one of the strangest places I've seen." "Yes, indeed," echoes Rudolph. "It is." "Speak gently, brambling child," says a fair woman walking by, in reprimand. (text-colour:lime)[While in a town, each hero may Rest, Pray and Train once per visit, and Shop and Trade as much as they can pay for. Traveling to a town does not consume your movement for your turn or end your turn unless specifically stated by an event.] [[Return->Main]]//''Dragon Clan Karst''// <div class="art art-town-dragon-clan-karst"></div> (Not written yet.) [[Return->Main]]//''The Stone Facade''// <div class="art art-town-the-stone-facade"></div> (Not written yet.) [[Return->Main]]//''Ash'Zel''// <div class="art art-town-ashzel"></div> (Not written yet.) [[Return->Main]]//''Cloudpost''// <div class="art art-town-cloudpost"></div> (Not written yet.) [[Return->Main]][[Return->Main]]The first kipling grumbles something to his companion. "Need change prices. Too expensive." He returns his attention to you. "Thief in Tower," he says. "Pays us money to not tell anyone. But not pays enough. Go visit if you like." [[Enter the tower->Sand3]] [[No thanks. (Leave)->Sand Leave]] The inside of the tower is merely a small room at the bottom and a single spiral ascending staircase. Light pours through the crystals with which the kiplings constructed this building, suffusing everything with a soft iridescence. Seemingly out of place at the top of the stairs is a solid oak door. [[Knock on the door -> Sand4]] [[Leave ->Sand Leave]] Your fist only knocks twice before the door lurches forward and crashes to the floor. Inside the room, a pale man sits cross-legged on a heap of other people's things: candlesticks, a saddle, a child's wooden horse, a church bell still on its rope. His skin is the white of old bone. The light from the crystal walls goes into him and doesn't come out the other side. He doesn't look at the door. He looks at you. "You're early," he says. His voice comes from somewhere just to the left of his mouth. (if: $bandit_location is true)[You know that pale shape. Balfour swore it moved like smoke on water. The White Bandit. ]"The kiplings sell my silence by the week," he says. "I sell theirs by the hour. Everything in this room belongs to someone who will never miss it. Take one thing, Trader, and we never met." [[Take one thing. (Draw a Tier II card. Doom +1.)->Sand4: Take one thing]] [["What are you?"->Sand4: What are you]] [[Leave him be. (End your turn.)->Sand4: Leave him be]]Three years ago, your older sister and best friend, Marla, told you of a faraway paradise called Traveler's Rest. She said the rest of your family was there and that she had to go and find them. She left the orphanage a month later and was never heard from again. You're determined to find out what became of her. To win: discover Marla's fate at Traveler's Rest. Locations F, G, H, I, and Z are off-limits for this scenario. Starting location: Hearthhome Starting Legacy Points: none. Setup: Set an elite token at "4" and "10" on the Doom track. Do not place the boss token. (set: $scenarioA to 1) Set the black "You Lose" token at "15" on the Doom track. If you reach 15 Doom this scenario, you lose. (set: $scenario to 1, $eliteAt to (a: 4, 10), $doomLimit to 15) [[Continue->Main]]//''Traveler's Rest''// <div class="art art-town-travelers-rest"></div> (if: $scenario is 1)[(set: $trVisited to true)] You’ve heard rumors that Traveler’s Rest is some sort of paradise. When you arrive, it is neither overly opulent nor destitute. Instead, what strikes you is a series of large, sequential terraces filled with water that seems to stream from the mountainside. The natural aquifers are outfitted with pipes that divert water to many acres of farmland, where people are hard at work tending to the soil. The landscape is dotted with cottages, and smoke drifts from the top of a large central yurt. “Traders are most welcome,” says an older woman, approaching. “For those looking to settle down, there is always room at the farms or in our trade houses.” (if: $scenario is 1)[ [[Ask about Marla->Traveler's Rest: Marla]] ] (text-colour:lime)[While in a town, each hero may Rest, Pray and Train once per visit, and Shop and Trade as much as they can pay for. Traveling to a town does not consume your movement for your turn or end your turn unless specifically stated by an event.] [[Return->Main]]//''Donalyn's Wall''// <div class="art art-town-donalyns-wall"></div> Towering beyond the confines of your imagination, this massive city sits cradled in Mount Theras's bosom. Its many-tiered layout houses at least a hundred thousand souls, mostly human, who thrive under the stewardship of Lord Donalyn and Lady Eriel. As you approach the gates, steel-clad knights salute you. "Humanity welcomes you, Trader, to the Last Bastion of Light in the east. You will find safety and comfort in these walls. Should you decide to venture forth to ply your wares, beware the Deadlands and all that lies beyond; that way lies only ruin." (if: $scenario is 1)[You note three posters hung prominently near the guard’s post. They read: <div class="art art-missing-poster"></div> ''Missing: Sami of Hearthhome'' ''Missing: Eric of Hearthhome'' ''Wanted: Marla of Hearthhome'' An eerie chill settles over you.] (text-colour:lime)[While in a town, each hero may Rest, Pray and Train once per visit, and Shop and Trade as much as they can pay for. Traveling to a town does not consume your movement for your turn or end your turn unless specifically stated by an event.] [[Return->Main]]//''The Woman at the Well''// <div class="art art-maiden"></div> In the deep of the plains, where rolling hills merge into flat expanses of nothing, a woman sits by a solitary well, looking wistful as she stares into its depths. She wears a worn black dress, and you hear her humming a sad tune to herself. Seeking to slake your thirst after a long march, you approach. "Do not bother stopping here, Traders," she says in a raspy voice, "for the well has run dry." You approach the well and look inside, surprised to see that it is filled with cool, blue water. [[Question the maiden.]] [[Drink from the well.]] //''Perfect Day''// <div class="art art-perfect"></div> Grassy plains stretch before you, and the open blue sky beckons in welcome. "It's a perfect day," remarks Thistle. "I'll say," says Rudolph. He chomps noisily on a carrot. You sigh contentedly, excited for the journey ahead. You can only hope that every day passes so peacefully. (text-colour:cyan)[Each hero gains 2 XP.] (text-colour:red)[Each hero heals 3 WP.] [[End your turn.->Main]](set: $xp to it + 2)"But the well is filled with water!" protests Rudolph. "No, it is not," says the woman. "But it really is," says Thistle plaintively. You entreat the woman to look. "I will not." [[Try to convince her. (Medium Wisdom check)->(Medium WIS) Try to convince her.]] [[Drink from the well and leave her be.->Drink from the well.]]Not to be deterred by her proclamations, you begin filling pails and passing out water. "I said the well is empty," she cries, but you ignore her and press on. The cool drink refreshes you, but renders the woman mute. If there was any conversation to be had, the time has passed. After several attempts at dialogue, you carry on, leaving the silent woman to her thoughts. (text-colour:cyan)[Each hero gains 1 XP.] (text-colour:red)[Each hero heals 3 WP.] [[End your turn.->Main]](set: $xp to it + 1)You argue with the woman, but she stubbornly refuses to see reason. She eventually pleads that you leave her be and not touch the water. Sighing, you settle for the water in your waterskins and make to leave. (text-colour:cyan)[Each hero gains 1 XP.] [[End your turn.->Main]](set: $xp to it + 1)You note the mournful look in her eyes as she hums her tune. The setting sun frames her silhouette, until she appears as black as her garb; you look on, contemplating what could drive a person to such a state. "Perhaps you have lost something precious," you finally say. You know as you speak the words that they are true; you wait for her confirmation. At her tepid nod, you continue. "But the well is not yet dry. I can see you are parched. Have a drink." "What do you know, Trader?" she asks, voice suddenly sharp. "I know only my craft: that of trading," you reply. "And what will you give me for my grief?" "I cannot replace something priceless," you say. "Nor would I seek to." "Then of what use are you?" "I will share with you my quiet company; in exchange, you may share your grief," you offer. Saying no more, you sit beside her and watch the last bit of sun dip below the rolling hills. Rudolph fills a cup from the well and hands it to the woman. Hesitantly, she drinks, then falls into silence. Before long, the day is mostly gone. Perhaps you imagine it, but some of the shadows in her eyes are gone as well. Eventually, you make to leave. She presses something into your hands, and kisses your cheek. "You have given me much, Trader," she says, then bids you farewell. (text-colour:cyan)[Each hero gains 1 XP.] (text-colour:green)[Draw from the top of the equipment deck until you reveal a Tier I card. Keep it, and put the other cards you revealed on the bottom of the deck.] [[End your turn.->Main]](set: $xp to it + 1)You've spent enough time in forests to know which way is up, down, left, right, and so forth. And you manage to surprise everyone with the haste with which you reach a clearing where the fallen dirigible lies. There, a startling scene unfolds. Engineers in Donalyn's livery cower beneath their downed vessel, while two battle-worn soldiers face a fearsome foe. "What should we do, boss?" asks Thistle, looking scared. [[Aid the soldiers. (Draw the top card of the Forest elite deck and fight it.)->sailfight]] [[Allow them to handle it themselves.->sailditch]] //''The Crystal Spires''// <div class="art art-spires"></div> Another day has passed, but the stars have seen fit to give you sufficient light to press onwards. The journey is silent as you make your way carefully through the forest until all of you stop at an odd sight. Several crystal spires rise from the earth, jutting out like fangs from a wolf. The light plays in them, creating a glittering facade and a mysterious aura. Thistle scratches her head nervously. "Oh, I don't know about this, boss," she says. Meanwhile, Rudolph's eyes seem to light up. "You don't see something like this every day. We've got to check them out," he says excitedly. [[Inspect the spires briefly.]] [[Decide to make camp among the spires.]] [[Pass on, leaving the spires behind.]]You reckon it's as good a place as any to bed down for the night, and you stop the carts within the glow of the spires. There is a holiness to them that begs some sort of reverence, but you're far too tired to do more than pay your silent respects. In the dead of the night, you awaken with a pounding headache, and your companions sit up as well. "Boss," says Thistle. "I don't feel right." "We need to leave right away," concurs Rudolph. As inconvenient as this is, and exhausted as you all are, you cannot help but agree. You rouse yourselves and leave the spires behind. Their memory fades in short order, but not before they elicit some strange growth within you. (text-colour:magenta)[Doom +1.] (text-colour:orange)[Each hero raises their max WP by 5 for the rest of this run.] [[End your turn.->Main]](set: $doom to it + 1)"Discretion is the better part of valor," you declare, "or something like that." "That's right," says Thistle. "Ain't no way a giant crystal-spire-monster-hungry-thingy is gonna eat me today. Hmph!" She crosses her arms defiantly. As if on cue, the earth roils and bucks beneath you, and what appears to be a giant crystal-spire-monster-hungry-thingy emerges, jaws agape, ready to devour. "Ah, shucks," says Thistle. (text-colour:cyan)[Each hero gains 3 XP.] (text-colour:purple)[Search the Forest enemy deck for the Chromatic Dragon Whelp and fight it.] [[End your turn.->Heroes fell]](set: $xp to it + 3)They seem to form no consistent pattern; rather, they are birthed from the earth as haphazardly as trees, wrought in nature's unordered majesty. Up close, you grow silent, a sense of reverence falling over you. "Let us not overstay our welcome," says Rudolph. "Our worn state feels somewhat offensive to this place." You nod in agreement. Shortly thereafter, you leave and cannot help but ponder the mysteries of this world. (text-colour:cyan)[Each hero gains 1 XP.] [[End your turn.->Main]](set: $xp to it + 1)//''The Shadow Wolves''// <div class="art art-wolves"></div> At night, the eyes of wolves glitter in the dark, like stars in the sky. You can see them, tiny points of light, perhaps several miles from your camp, visible despite the great distance. "Hollowlight wolves," says Rudolph, pondering. "They shouldn't be this far from the forest, though." "I sure hope they don't like chomping on nature spirits," says Thistle nervously. "Oh no. I bet I'm delicious. I bet my bones taste like strawberries or pumpkin pie. Or maybe jambalaya." Rudolph shakes his head. "They're far too intelligent and competent predators to waste their time chasing prey like us for food. I suspect for them to be this far away from the Hollowlight Expanse, they are either here on orders, or else we are close to encroaching on something they protect. That said, I don't think they're too proud to accept offerings. What should we do?" [[Leave an offering. (Each hero sacrifices 2 Food.)->Leave an offering. (Sacrifice 2 Food.)]] [[Set up an ambush. (Easy Power check)->(Easy POW) Set up an ambush.]] [[Attempt to obscure your trail.]] [[Try to barter with the wolves. (Hard Savoir faire check)->(Hard SAV) Try to barter with the wolves.]] The easiest course of action, you decide, is to pay off your pursuers. "Unscrupulous types like bribes," declares Thistle confidently, "especially if those bribes are delicious food. I consider myself full of scruples, but things change when I see a pie." She then pulls a stick out of her wild hair, inspects it, shrugs, and puts it back in. "Strange elemental girl," you mutter to yourself, while side-eyeing her. "I heard that!" she harrumphs. "I know," you say. Discounting Thistle's supernatural senses for the moment, you take your offering, bundle it carefully in paper, and tie a ribbon on it for good measure. "I'll trade this package to you, Mr. or Mrs. Wolf, in return for not eating me in my sleep," you say to no one in particular. With that settled, you return to camp and lie down for a restless night. Over the next few days, it becomes clear that your pursuers have accepted the deal, as they disappear from your trail. (text-colour:cyan)[Each hero gains 1 XP.] (text-colour:green)[Each hero sacrifices 2 Food.] (text-colour:red)[Each hero heals 6 WP.] [[End your turn.->Main]](set: $xp to it + 1, $food to (max: 0, it - 2 * $heroes))The next morning, you press on until you find a gully with a small stream running through it. Carefully guiding your cart and pack animals down the bank, you splash into the knee-high water and work your way upstream until you reach a shallow alcove, where you hide out for a day. The process is long but effective. Sure enough, when you set out again, the wolves seem to have lost your scent. (text-colour:magenta)[Doom +1.] (text-colour:cyan)[Each hero gains 2 XP.] [[End your turn.->Main]](set: $doom to it + 1, $xp to it + 2)You suddenly recollect that the Uktali have a saying: "Like trying to barter with wolves." It roughly translates to "a really bad idea." As soon as you approach, the wolves begin snarling and snapping, and then lunge for you. After a long, bloody affair, you finally manage to ward them off, but not without a cost to your body. (text-colour:red)[You lose 10 WP.] [[End your turn.->Main]]Up close, the creatures have startlingly black fur and brilliant blue eyes glowing with light. Against all odds, conceivable logic, common sense, and much to the utter stupefaction of your companions, you begin a dialogue with the wolves. Through a series of yips, yowls, growls, some spontaneous breakdancing, and a little bit of rock-paper-scissors, you seem to come to some sort of accord. The strange beasts pad away silently into the night. "Even I didn't see that coming," muses Thistle. "I thought for sure you were mincemeat." "'Wolf Whisperer,'" says Rudolph, eyes wide in awe. (set: $supported to true, $wolfPack to true)(text-colour:orange)[The pack comes to an agreement with you, abandons its former masters, and lends you its aid. Your party is now Supported.] (text-colour:orange)[Wolf Pack Support: in the first round of every fight, one enemy of your choice becomes Vulnerable 1.] [[End your turn.->Main]]//''Sunken City''// <div class="art art-town-sunken-city"></div> (Not written yet.) [[Return->Main]]Roll Wisdom (Medium, 4 or higher), then pick your result. (dropdown: bind $rollText, "Choose...", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6") (link-repeat: "Submit roll")[ (if: $rollText is "4" or $rollText is "5" or $rollText is "6")[(go-to: "The Maiden's Reply (3)")] (else-if: $rollText is "1" or $rollText is "2" or $rollText is "3")[(go-to: "The Maiden's Reply")] (else:)[Please choose a number first.] ]Roll Power (Easy, 3 or higher), then pick your result. (dropdown: bind $rollText, "Choose...", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6") (link-repeat: "Submit roll")[ (if: $rollText is "3" or $rollText is "4" or $rollText is "5" or $rollText is "6")[(go-to: "amb2")] (else-if: $rollText is "1" or $rollText is "2")[(go-to: "amb1")] (else:)[Please choose a number first.] ]Roll Savoir faire (Hard, 5 or higher), then pick your result. (dropdown: bind $rollText, "Choose...", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6") (link-repeat: "Submit roll")[ (if: $rollText is "5" or $rollText is "6")[(go-to: "Wolf reply 2")] (else-if: $rollText is "1" or $rollText is "2" or $rollText is "3" or $rollText is "4")[(go-to: "Wolf reply 1")] (else:)[Please choose a number first.] ]Rudolph has a bright idea to cover yourselves with mud and launch yourselves at your foes like things from the swamp. The problem is that there isn't much mud to be seen — until you spot some squelching terrain near a streambank. You proceed with the plan, feeling less and less certain each passing moment. When at last the strange, dark beasts with glowing eyes arrive, you hurl yourselves at them, yelling loud war cries. Your sudden appearance frightens them, but only for a moment, as the slippery mud provides little traction. Your party begins slipping and falling, and slipping and falling again in the mud, cursing all the while. Your weapons don't seem to stay in your hands, and eventually you just give up and sit there in the mud, defeated. The silver lining is that the wolves don't quite know what to make of you. They turn their heads cockeyed in quizzical expressions, and eventually you see them give up and begin rifling through your belongings in your cart before departing. You get the sense that whatever display you managed was so embarrassing that they decided to take pity on you. (text-colour:green)[Each hero loses 2 Food.] (text-colour:red)[Each hero loses 2 WP.] [[End your turn.->Main]](set: $food to (max: 0, it - 2 * $heroes))There aren't many places to hide out on these rolling plains, but a particularly large hill with a stone overlook gives you the cover you need. When at last the wolves reach your position, you launch your offensive, and their instinctive response is to cower and flee. (text-colour:cyan)[Each hero gains 3 XP.] [[End your turn.->Main]](set: $xp to it + 3)//''Burning Home''// <div class="art art-fire"></div> As you pass through a small hamlet, the sick stench of smoldering dung catches your attention, right before the telltale plume of smoke alerts you to what is going on. You press forward to see frantic townspeople tossing buckets of water at a burning townhouse. A terrible feeling settles in your gut as you put two and two together. "Trader," says an elderly man approaching, "I am afraid this is no time for commerce. We have a crisis on our hands." "Is there anyone in there?" you ask. "No, thank God. It was empty when it caught fire," he says. Suddenly, you hear a cry coming from inside the house, and a jolt of alarm goes through you. There is no time for deliberation. The flames are licking higher and higher. Truly, if there is someone in there, someone must act before the heat grows fierce enough to bar entry and exit. Several men have paused, hearing the cries. One or two young men look as if they're about to dive into the building themselves. [[Run in yourself and try to find the source of the cries. (Hard Savoir faire check)->Burning Home: Rush in]] [[Help with the water line and the buckets.->Burning Home: Bucket line]]//''Wind in My Sails''// <div class="art art-sails"></div> "Look! Look!" says Thistle. "Up there!" You crane your neck to see, high above the treetops, a large zeppelin floating through the sky. "An airbus!" exclaims Rudolph. "It's probably heading back towards Donalyn's Wall." He looks proud of the rare technical marvel, as if humanity's achievement were his own as well. Suddenly, a plume of smoke rises from the vehicle, and you see it descending slowly until it dips below the trees. Looks of concern populate your crew. "Well, boss?" asks Thistle. "Should we investigate?" The zeppelin could be far off the beaten track; if so, it would take you considerable time to reach it. [[Locate the fallen zeppelin. (Medium Wisdom check)->(Medium WIS) Locate the fallen zeppelin.]] [[Continue with your journey.]] //''Rumors''// <div class="art art-rumors"></div> A cloudy day brings you to a fork in the road where an old man is muttering to himself. "As big as my palm," he says. "As big as my palm," he says again. As you approach, he jumps, startled. "Didn't see you there," he says nervously. "What's as big as your palm?" you ask. "Oh, I didn't say that," he says, shaking his finger. "I didn't say there was any piece of treasure as big as my palm. I did not say that. I did not say that there was a gem as big as my palm or bigger off the Azure Coast. I certainly did not say that." "If you say so," you say uncertainly. "I did NOT say so," he says. "No, I did not. Certainly not." "All right then," you reply. "Okay then," he says. Realizing the conversation isn't going any further, you exchange an awkward farewell and begin your journey again, musing at the strange encounter. Thistle approaches you, whispering conspiratorially, "What did he say?" You just shrug. (set: $palmTreasure to true) [[End your turn.->Main]] You recall that the zeppelins from Donalyn's Wall are manned with competent engineers and have a small security force. They should be more than capable of handling whatever problems have arisen with the zeppelin. Regardless, you simply don't have the time to investigate. You'll have to leave them to their own devices so that you can press on. (text-colour:cyan)[Each hero gains 1 XP.] [[End your turn.->Main]](set: $xp to it + 1)Roll Wisdom (Medium, 4 or higher), then pick your result. (dropdown: bind $rollText, "Choose...", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6") (link-repeat: "Submit roll")[ (if: $rollText is "4" or $rollText is "5" or $rollText is "6")[(go-to: "sail2")] (else-if: $rollText is "1" or $rollText is "2" or $rollText is "3")[(go-to: "sail1")] (else:)[Please choose a number first.] ]The trail to the fallen dirigible is as arduous as predicted. A series of winding trails and loop-de-loops through increasingly dense thickets finally leads you to a clearing. There, a startling scene unfolds. Engineers in Donalyn's livery cower beneath their downed vessel, while two battle-worn soldiers face a fearsome foe. "What should we do, boss?" asks Thistle, looking scared. (text-colour:magenta)[Doom +1.] [[Aid the soldiers. (Draw the top card of the Forest elite deck and fight it.)->sailfight]] [[Allow them to handle it themselves.->sailditch]](set: $doom to it + 1)"To arms!" you cry, and charge into battle. (if: $heroes is 4)[(text-colour:purple)[Four heroes: also draw 1 enemy from the Forest enemy deck. It fights beside the elite, acts after it, and pays its printed drop.] ](text-colour:lime)[Select the appropriate option based on the outcome of your fight: ][[You triumphed over your foe.]] [[You were defeated.]]"This foe is beyond us," you whisper. "We can do nothing." You beat a hasty retreat, feeling chagrined at your cowardice. (text-colour:magenta)[Doom +1.] [[End your turn.->Main]](set: $doom to it + 1)You emerge blood-soaked and exhausted, but victorious. "Traders! Here in the depths of these woods? You're a godsend. I thought for sure we were goners," says the captain, approaching with an outstretched hand. His two engineers crawl out from beneath the airbus looking shell-shocked; the battle-worn soldiers give you tired salutes. "You have done us a great service," says the captain, "and it is only right that we repay you. But unfortunately, we have little to give. Take this coin... and, once we've fixed the zeppelin, we could offer you free passage to Donalyn's Wall, if you desire." Rudolph's eyes light up. "Can the airbus take our animals and wagons too?" you ask. "Yes, indeed," says the captain. "This vehicle is Donalyn's finest." "Amazing," Rudolph breathes. (text-colour:green)[Collect the elite's printed rewards.] (text-colour:yellow)[Each hero gains 2 gold.] [[Accept passage to Donalyn's Wall. (Move your party to Donalyn's Wall. End your turn.)->Heroes fell]] [[Decline politely. (End your turn.)->Heroes fell]](set: $gold to it + 2 * $heroes)When you wake, you are aboard the airbus, which has been patched together and is limping through the sky. The two soldiers are sitting across from you, and they look considerably worse than you feel. "You held it off long enough for us to get her airborne," one of them says. "We weren't about to leave you for the crows." They set you down at the forest's edge and apologize that they can't take you any farther before the airbus sputters off toward home. (text-colour:orange)[This defeat does not end your run. Every hero gets back up with 25% of their max WP. Fallen heroes still add Doom as usual.] [[End your turn.->Heroes fell]]//''Crowded Watering Hole''// <div class="art art-water"></div> Watering holes are few and far between in the Deadlands, and so when you do find one, it is crowded with dusty travelers, each with their own saddled riding lynx. The feline creatures eye your carthorses with a certain amount of curiosity. You notice one pad over in an attempt to playfully bat at its tail before its owner reins it back. Most of the travelers wear shrouds that cover their faces to keep the dust out and obscure their identity, but you guess that they are either couriers or at the behest of some rich and powerful folk. They give you a wide berth as you approach, some muttering "Traders" under their breath with a certain amount of respect. Others seem to be sizing you up. They appear intent on leaving you to your business if you leave them to theirs. It seems almost too good to be true. (set: $bandits to true) (text-colour:red)[Each hero heals half of their max WP.] [[End your turn.->Main]] //''The Old Man and the Sea''// <div class="art art-sea"></div> There is a man on a boat in the sea. His face is all old lines, weathered, worn, and cracked by time or circumstance. His eyes are intent on his fishing line, bobbing in the shallows. He glances up as you pass by, and his eyes light up. He smiles, lines transforming his face from concentration to welcome, and he waves. "One old man to another," calls Rudolph from your skiff, waving back, "what does the sea have to say today?" "She says, 'Good things are coming,'" replies the man. "But only if I am patient." He licks his lips as the line gives a little tug, but nothing comes of it. "Are the fish biting?" asks Rudolph. "Oh, yes. Caught a big'un the other day, and I've had a few nibbles this morning, but I'm sure any day now I'm gonna catch the second-best prize." Thistle's ears perk up. "The second-best prize? What's that?" she asks. "Why, the biggest fish you've ever seen, young little miss," says the man, "with golden scales, said to bless any man or woman who catches him and throws him back in the sea." Thistle folds her arms skeptically. "Huh. That sounds like a load of baloney to me," she says. [[Listen to the old man's stories.]] [[Leave the old man and be on your way.->Leave the old man to be on your way.]] There is a feeling of change in the air, though you're not sure if the world has changed or if you have. [[Leave. (Each hero raises one attribute by 1.)->Old Man: Leave]] [[Fish. It feels like a good fishing spot. (Medium Power, Wisdom and Savoir faire checks)->Old Man: Fish]]"Oh, I assure you, the golden fish is real. Saw him myself when I was just a boy," says the old man. "I've been searching for him ever since. Just to say hi one more time." "Does that mean you already caught him?" "Well," says the man, scratching his scraggly beard. "Caught is a strong word, but I was fortunate enough to be able to give him back to the sea." You were about to ask him what blessing the fish gave him, but Thistle gets ahead of you. "So if this magical fish is the second-best prize, what's the grand prize?" she asks. At that question, the man goes silent, until you only hear the lapping of waves against the distant shore. The world grows very quiet, and your thoughts, buzzing as they often are, seem to notice the ambient stillness and silence themselves. You observe a few errant thoughts, like misbehaving children still running wild, and though you are tempted to chase them, you let them go. Then it seems as if all the world is alive. There is a warmth to everything, even to the cool breeze, and you feel something stirring in your heart, like a memory of something long past but still present: a flame that continues to burn across the eons of time and timelessness. You find yourself closing your eyes and imagining a field filled with amber wheat and emerald grass and a singular well. Then, as sure as the sun rises, you hear a voice: //I am not the grass or the seas, the skies or the breeze. I am not one of these things, and yet I am all of these things. I am love in the silence, or silence in the moments between music, or a well's depth hidden by shadow: something present but deeper, implied by the physical and cognitive world, yet not of it, nor defined by it. I am the mystery of life, the song in your heart, the quiescent state where no ''thing'' exists, yet all are one. I love you, and I am with you always, until you return home to Me. // You pass by, as do the breaths and the moments, until at last you open your eyes and see that the sun is beginning to dip below the horizon. The day is almost past, and you notice your companions stirring, awakening as if from a slumber as well. You look for the old man, but he is gone. [[What happened?->So that was the grand prize?]]You wish the old man luck and push on, and he waves you off without taking his eyes from the water. "Good things are coming," Rudolph mutters, chomping on a carrot. "If I had a copper for every time someone told me that..." "You'd have a copper," says Thistle. As you sail away, you catch a flash of gold beneath the waves out of the corner of your eye, but when you turn to look, the old man is still sitting alone with his line in the water. [[End your turn.->Main]]"Living," he says sheepishly, rubbing the back of his head. "Once you get to know the kiplings, they're not so bad," he adds. "I thought you went north with Marla?" Rudolph says. Martin's eyes grow distant. "I was supposed to," he says. [[What happened?]] "We were supposed to go to Traveler's Rest. Most of us wanted to go up the coast, where it's safer, but you know Marla. She insisted on the most direct route. We traveled past Donalyn's Wall to the wastes beyond. "The Deadlands are aptly named. On our first day, we saw a tornado the size of a mountain. On the second, we saw strange figures in robes prowling at night. After that, we knew we needed to turn back or die. So we left. I decided that was enough travel for me; the kiplings here took a shine to me... or maybe just my cooking. They treat me as their own. So here I am." [[What happened to the rest?]] "There were five of us: Sami, Dietrich, Eric, Marla, and I. Most everyone else stayed at Donalyn's Wall. But Marla, she was determined. You know how pig-headed she gets. She couldn't be talked out of this mad quest for paradise. We tried to tell her it was unsafe. If you haven't heard from her like she promised, it's likely she died in those wastes." [[Thank you, Martin.]]Martin clasps your shoulder. "I know how much you cared for her. I'm sorry. If I could advise you on one thing, it would be: don't make the same mistake she did. Don't go into the Deadlands. You won't survive." [[I have no choice.]] [[We'll find another way.]]"I'm afraid there's no choice. We can't waste any more time. We have to take the most direct route, and so we will pass through the Deadlands." Martin spends an inordinate amount of time trying to convince you otherwise, but he sees you cannot be swayed. "At the very least, take these items. The kiplings won't mind their absence," he says. You thank him and bid him farewell, and prepare yourself for the dangers of the road. (set: $scenarioA to 0) (text-colour:green)[Each hero draws from the top of the equipment deck until they reveal a Tier I card and keeps it. Put the other cards revealed on the bottom of the deck.] [[Return->Main]]"Finally, someone speaking sense. You're making the right decision, friend. If you must find her, or find this mythical paradise that she sought, it is surely safer to travel up the coast or through the forest. "Please be safe. We cannot lose another member of the family." He presses something into your hands. "Take these items. The kiplings won't mind their absence." You spend a few more hours talking of less dire topics, but your quest weighs on you. Eventually, you thank him and bid him farewell, and prepare yourself for the dangers of the road. (set: $scenarioA to 0) (text-colour:green)[Each hero draws from the top of the equipment deck until they reveal a Tier I card and keeps it. Put the other cards revealed on the bottom of the deck.] [[Return->Main]]//''The Inscription''// <div class="art art-inscript"></div> In the middle of a forest clearing, you come across a worn stone pedestal with a poem inscribed on its surface: "My eyes are green, sparkling Replete with God's vision I see the cosmic puzzle Like spider strands woven Across the silken sky No labyrinthine maze But holiness and order Living all around me A mystery to unravel As diamonds to my Eye The Cosmos, She conspires To hold me in Her arms All the world's Her cradle She whispers to me sweetly To soar, to swoon, to fly Father-Mother, hear me Yearning to come home, Hope, do not depart me, I Am a prodigal child Returning unto nigh." There are flowers laid on the pedestal, and it smells of sweet perfume. There is a reverence to this place that you feel words would sully. As you depart silently, it feels as though the presence of evil in the world has lessened a bit. (text-colour:magenta)[Doom −2.] [[End your turn.->Main]](set: $doom to (max: 0, it - 2))//''Elusive Prey''// <div class="art art-prey"></div> The snapping of branches alerts you to the presence of an unwelcome visitor: an Uktali elf, covered in war paint, approaches. "Traders," he says in the strange, flowing Elven tongue, "we have you surrounded. Lay down your arms and we will do you no harm." "Why should we parley with savages?" you retort. The elf smiles back lazily. "If you do not, it will be the death of you. Do not think your status as Traders protects you in these lands. The world beyond the forest may view you as just, but we view you as a nuisance. Come now, lay down your arms, and I will not touch you. You see, we seek an elusive prey, and we need your aid." [[Lay down your weapons.->Lay down your weapons]] [[To arms!]] "I'm glad some of your kind see sense," says the elf. "We are on the hunt for a wild creature who is called //Twrch Trwyth// in our tongue. He is a great beast, perhaps three times the size of a man, and nestled in his bristles, just behind his ears, are the sacred comb, razors, and scissors of our high priestess. Retrieve these items, and you will be rewarded beyond your imagination." [[We will join your hunt. (Hard Wisdom, Savoir faire and Power checks)->(Very difficult SAV, POW, WIS) We will join your hunt.]] [[We are weary from our journey, and we fear this task is beyond us.]] (text-colour:purple)[Search the Forest enemy deck for two random Uktali cards and fight them.] If you win this combat: (text-colour:cyan)[Each hero gains 2 XP.] (text-colour:green)[Draw from the top of the equipment deck until you reveal three Tier II cards. Keep one, and put the rest on the bottom of the deck.] [[End your turn.->Heroes fell]]"Hmm," says the elf. "Perhaps there is wisdom in knowing one's limits. Very well, Traders! I shall let you leave with your lives. But know, if you return to these woods, there will be no fortune to greet you, only my spear and the fury of my brethren." (text-colour:cyan)[Each hero gains 2 XP.] [[End your turn.->Main]] (set: $xp to it + 2)Roll Wisdom (Hard, 5 or higher), then pick your result. (dropdown: bind $rollText, "Choose...", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6") (link-repeat: "Submit roll")[ (if: $rollText is "5" or $rollText is "6")[(go-to: "combwin")] (else-if: $rollText is "1" or $rollText is "2" or $rollText is "3" or $rollText is "4")[(go-to: "combfail")] (else:)[Please choose a number first.] ]You track the boar to a grotto where it drinks from crystalline waters. As it does, the water turns an inky black, and the pig snorts in pleasure. "The pig contains an evil spirit," says the elf. "He poisons our lands. Do not bother trying to harm it, for as long as it has the sacred relics, it is invincible. You must be clever, and crafty, and sneaky, as your kind is." "Wow," says Rudolph. "Elves," you find yourself muttering. Eventually, you devise a plan with a fishing line and a hook. With a great deal of difficulty, you manage to creep behind the boar and snag the comb. "Impressive," says the elf. [[Go after the razors. (Hard Savoir faire check)->Elusive prey: Razors roll]]You track the boar to a grotto where it drinks from crystalline waters. As it does, the water turns an inky black, and the pig snorts in pleasure. "The pig contains an evil spirit," says the elf. "He poisons our lands. Do not bother trying to harm it, for as long as it has the sacred relics, it is invincible. You must be clever, and crafty, and sneaky, as your kind is." "Wow," says Rudolph. "Elves," you find yourself muttering. Eventually, you devise a plan with a fishing line and a hook. With a great deal of difficulty, you manage to creep behind the boar and reach for the comb. Unfortunately, at the last moment, your fingers twitch, snagging a bit of the boar's snout instead of the comb. You scrape the hook along its ear, and it squeals in pain and charges you. "I knew I should not have relied on Traders," says the elf, his tone disappointed. "Be gone from my sight." (text-colour:red)[Each hero loses 6 WP.] [[End your turn.->Main]]//''Manna from Heaven''// <div class="art art-manna"></div> Your feet feel like lead; your bones like jelly; and your head like sand. In short, you are tired. "Boss, can we stop? Puh-leaaaaaase?" Thistle practically begs you. You are about to protest, when suddenly a miracle occurs: an abandoned campsite appears on the horizon, replete with victuals of all kinds. There are dried sausages, berries, bread, libations, and more. The elemental girl does a complete backflip, then sprints forward, inspecting the scene. "It's real! It's not an illusion. It was not summoned here by an evil wizard bent on revenge. There's no catches. No gimmicks. It's just foooooood!" [[Make camp for the night. (Every hero heals to full WP. Doom +1.)->Manna from Heaven: Make camp]] [[Press on. (Each hero gains 1 XP.)->Manna from Heaven: Press on]]You don't need to be told twice. Within the hour, you have circled the wagons and fed the animals, and Thistle is already on her third sausage, while Rudolph works his way through the berries slowly, one at a time, as if he suspects he doesn't deserve them. Whoever left the feast never comes back for it, and nobody in your party is in any hurry to wonder why. You sleep soundly through the night and well into the next morning, which costs you a day on the road. (text-colour:red)[Every hero heals to full WP.] (text-colour:magenta)[Doom +1.] [[End your turn.->Main]](set: $doom to it + 1)"We can't afford to lose a day," you say, and Thistle lets out a long groan of protest. She stuffs as many sausages into her pockets as they will hold, and then a few more into her hair, while Rudolph pretends not to notice. "A wise choice," he says, around a mouthful of bread that he definitely did not pack. You set off again with full pockets, though your legs still ache from the road. (text-colour:cyan)[Each hero gains 1 XP.] [[End your turn.->Main]](set: $xp to it + 1)Roll Savoir faire (Hard, 5 or higher), then pick your result. (dropdown: bind $rollText, "Choose...", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6") (link-repeat: "Submit roll")[ (if: $rollText is "5" or $rollText is "6")[(go-to: "Elusive prey: Razors won")] (else-if: $rollText is "1" or $rollText is "2" or $rollText is "3" or $rollText is "4")[(go-to: "Elusive prey: Razors failed")] (else:)[Please choose a number first.] ]The razors are tangled deep in the bristles behind the boar's ear, where no fishing line will reach. Someone is going to have to get close. That someone is you. You approach the beast cautiously. "What magnificent, uh, tusks you have," you try, as the beast's nostrils flare. The boar's ears twitch. It leans into your hand like a dog that wants a scratch, and you oblige, and when your hand comes away, the razors come with it. Thistle stage-whispers to the elf. "Boss just flirted with a pig." "Truly, the swine has been wooed by your leader's seductive prowess," returns the elf. Suddenly, the boar rears up to charge, snapping out of whatever juju you miraculously performed. [[Go after the scissors. (Hard Power check)->Elusive prey: Scissors roll]]The razors are tangled deep in the bristles behind the boar's ear, where no fishing line will reach. Someone is going to have to get close. That someone is you. You approach the beast cautiously. "What magnificent, uh, tusks you have," you try, as the beast's nostrils flare. The boar does not care for compliments. It charges. By the time you have untangled yourself from a thornbush, the beast is gone and the elf is turning the comb over in his hands. "One of three," he says. "I suppose that is more than I expected from Traders." (text-colour:red)[Each hero loses 6 WP.] (text-colour:cyan)[Each hero gains 1 XP.] [[End your turn.->Main]](set: $xp to it + 1)Roll Power (Hard, 5 or higher), then pick your result. (dropdown: bind $rollText, "Choose...", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6") (link-repeat: "Submit roll")[ (if: $rollText is "5" or $rollText is "6")[(go-to: "Elusive prey: Scissors won")] (else-if: $rollText is "1" or $rollText is "2" or $rollText is "3" or $rollText is "4")[(go-to: "Elusive prey: Scissors failed")] (else:)[Please choose a number first.] ]With nothing left to do but fight for your life, you crash your fist down on the boar's snout. Miraculously, the force of the blow knocks the scissors loose, and, more miraculously still, the boar is felled. Having recovered the three items, the elf appears surprised. "I was right to put my faith in you, Trader," he says. [[What is my reward?->Elusive prey: What is my reward?]]With nothing left to do but fight for your life, you crash your fist down on the boar's snout, but poor footing causes your blow to glance. It rampages, trampling over you and your party. The elf weighs the comb and razors in his hands, then looks to the trees where the boar disappeared. "Two of three," he says. "Not beyond my imagination, Traders. But not beneath it." He leaves you a small pouch and slips back into the forest. (text-colour:red)[Each hero loses 6 WP.] (text-colour:cyan)[Each hero gains 2 XP.] (text-colour:yellow)[Each hero gains 2 gold.] [[End your turn.->Main]](set: $xp to it + 2, $gold to it + 2 * $heroes)"Come! See! The priestess will want to reward you, Trader." He leads you on secret paths through the trees, and in no time you have reached the hallowed conclave of Sacred Silence. (text-colour:lime)[Move your party to Sacred Silence.] The high priestess resides in a temple high among the trees, crafted to blend into the wood around it. You ascend myriad steps until you are face to face with her, and you present her with her relics. "Trader, you were promised a reward. My daughter, Olwen, has been seeking a worthy champion. You may have her hand in marriage." A beautiful, pale-skinned elven woman steps forward, and seems to measure you, before nodding. Thistle makes a noise like a stepped-on cat. Rudolph has gone very still, in the manner of a man trying to become furniture. "Do you accept?" asks the high priestess. [[Accept Olwen's hand.->Elusive prey: Accept]] [[Decline.->Elusive prey: Decline]]You accept. As you do, you are drawn into the elvish woman's eyes, and you feel that something special has taken place. "Elvenkind have long memories. I do not recall meeting you, but I feel as if we have known each other before," she remarks, sounding puzzled. The wedding is held at dawn; before noon, the high priestess is ushering your party on its way, your elvish bride in tow. As you make to leave the bounds of Sacred Silence, the surrealness of what just occurred sets in. You stand still for a moment, stupefied, before a playful smack shatters your reverie. "Come, Trader. Let us depart. I am excited to travel the world with you," says a grinning Olwen. (set: $married to true, $spouse to "Olwen", $spouseShe to "she", $spouseHer to "her", $spouseHim to "her") (text-colour:orange)[You are now Married, and Olwen joins your caravan.] (text-colour:green)[Draw from the top of the equipment deck until you reveal two Tier III cards. Keep one, and put the rest on the bottom of the deck.] (text-colour:cyan)[Each hero gains 3 XP.] (text-colour:yellow)[Each hero gains 3 gold.] ''Elvish dowry.'' Choose one benefit for the rest of this run: * Earn double Legacy Points at the end of this run. * +6 max WP. * Upgrade your damage die one size (d4 → d6 → d8 → d10 → d12). * Gain 2 Food and 1 each of Herbs, Materials, Gems and Exotic Goods right away. [[End your turn.->Main]](set: $xp to it + 3, $gold to it + 3 * $heroes, $food to it + 2, $herbs to it + 1, $materials to it + 1, $gems to it + 1, $exotic to it + 1)The temple goes very quiet, which in Sacred Silence is saying something. The hush is broken by the priestess, who nods. "As you wish, Trader," she says. "Better the harsh truth than a pleasant lie for my daughter. Take this, then, and go with our thanks." Outside, Rudolph claps you on the shoulder. He searches for words, but can't find any. Your journey continues. (text-colour:green)[Draw from the top of the equipment deck until you reveal two Tier III cards. Keep one, and put the rest on the bottom of the deck.] (text-colour:cyan)[Each hero gains 5 XP.] (text-colour:yellow)[Each hero gains 3 gold.] [[End your turn.->Main]](set: $xp to it + 5, $gold to it + 3 * $heroes)//''Just Resting''// <div class="art art-resting"></div> Half a mile off the coast, you spot a frogfolk floating on his back in the open water with his hands folded on his belly and his eyes closed, though there is no boat anywhere nearby that he could have come from. When you call out to him, he opens one eye. "Just resting," he says, and closes it again. A moment later, a fin cuts through the water some way behind him, followed by a second one. "Still resting," he calls, a little louder this time. [[Haul him aboard.->Just Resting: Haul him aboard]] [[Leave him to his rest. (End your turn.)->Main]]You haul him over the side, and he climbs aboard dripping wet but with all the dignity of a lord. "I had them right where I wanted them," he says, referring to the sharks. He rides with you as far as the next anchorage and hops off without a word of thanks, but on the deck where he was sitting, he has left a small, wet pouch. Inside are three pearls and a note in very careful handwriting: //I was not drowning.// (text-colour:cyan)[Each hero gains 1 XP.] (text-colour:green)[Gain 1 Gem.] [[End your turn.->Main]](set: $xp to it + 1, $gems to it + 1)//''The Cursed Potato''// <div class="art art-potato"></div> Half-buried in the sand at the bottom of a dry gully sits a rather large potato. Someone has stacked a little cairn of bones in front of it. Someone has also, quite recently, stuck a sign in the sand beside it. DO NOT TAKE THE POTATO. Beneath that, in smaller, shakier letters: DO NOT! [[Take the potato. (Draw a Tier II card. Doom +2.)->The Cursed Potato: Take it]] [[Leave it be. (End your turn.)->Main]]You pick up the potato. It has to be at least ten pounds. "This," you think, "is a MASSIVE potato." It's kind of spongy and squishy and you probably shouldn't eat it. Fortunately, underneath is an artifact of some worth. You take it, but are slightly disappointed that you can't make French fries with this potato like you wanted to. Meanwhile, the wind picks up ominously behind you. Oh, well. (text-colour:green)[Draw from the top of the equipment deck until you reveal a Tier II card. Keep it, and put the other cards you revealed on the bottom of the deck.] (text-colour:magenta)[Doom +2.] [[End your turn.->Main]](set: $doom to it + 2)//''The Polite Scarecrow''// <div class="art art-scarecrow"></div> At the edge of a wheat field stands a scarecrow with its arms out wide. It is very tall and thin and furred with moss, and as you pass, it says, very slowly, "Ex... cuse... me." On closer inspection, the scarecrow turns out to be a sylvan. He has been standing here for three weeks, because the farmer mistook him for a scarecrow and he thought it would be rude to say otherwise. "The... crows... are... terrible," he adds. "But... the... farmer... is... rather... pleased." [[Explain things to the farmer.->Scarecrow: The farmer]] [[Wish him well. (End your turn.)->Main]]//''Pen Pals''// <div class="art art-penpals"></div> A bottle bumps against your hull, corked and sealed with wax, and inside it is a letter written in a round, careful hand: //To whoever finds this: I am nine years old, and I live on a rock in the middle of the sea. Please write back and tell me about anywhere else.// Folded beneath it are a blank page and a stub of charcoal worn down to almost nothing. (link: "Write back, and return the bottle to the sea. (Each hero gains 1 XP.)")[(set: $xp to it + 1)(go-to: "Main")] (link: "Keep the bottle. It's a nice bottle. (Gain 1 Exotic Goods.)")[(set: $exotic to it + 1)(go-to: "Main")]//''Fresh Ice''// <div class="art art-ice"></div> In the middle of the wastes, a hundred miles from anywhere, a kipling sits under a tattered parasol behind a little wooden stall with a sign that reads: ICE. FRESH ICE. 1 GOLD. Sure enough, there is a copper basin full of clear ice sweating in the heat, though you can't see a well, a cart or a cellar anywhere that it could have come from. "Where does it come from?" you ask. "Ice come from ice," the kipling says proudly. While you are puzzling over this, you notice a faint snoring coming from somewhere behind the stall. (link: "Buy ice for the party. (Each hero pays 1 gold and heals 6 WP.)")[(set: $gold to (max: 0, it - 1 * $heroes))(go-to: "Main")] [[Do not ask about the snoring. (End your turn.)->Main]]//''The Foreign Poem''// <div class="art art-poem"></div> Along the beach on the Azure Coast, you see a man sitting alone. He stares out at the lapping waves, hands on his knees as if lost in thought. Beside him lies a leather-bound book, which he occasionally picks up, peruses, and sets back down. He nods at you as you approach, but does not say more. [[What are you doing?->The Foreign Poem: What are you doing?]] [[What's in the book?->The Foreign Poem: What's in the book?]] [[Bid him farewell. (Each hero gains 1 XP.)->The Foreign Poem: Farewell]]"Listening. Sometimes I imagine I can hear them too." He taps the book. "Church bells underneath the ocean... from a lost land sunk underwater." [[Like the mythical sunken city of the West?->The Foreign Poem: The sunken city]] (unless: (history:) contains "The Foreign Poem: What's in the book?")[ [[What's in the book?->The Foreign Poem: What's in the book?]] ] [[Bid him farewell. (Each hero gains 1 XP.)->The Foreign Poem: Farewell]]"No, that is a different place. An unfriendly and inhospitable one, or so I hear. There is no way in. I would not bother venturing there." (unless: (history:) contains "The Foreign Poem: What's in the book?")[ [[What's in the book?->The Foreign Poem: What's in the book?]] ] [[Bid him farewell. (Each hero gains 1 XP.)->The Foreign Poem: Farewell]]"It's poetry from a very faraway place. I found it when I was a child, and it is one of my most treasured possessions." [[Ask to read the book.->The Foreign Poem: Read the book]] (unless: (history:) contains "The Foreign Poem: What are you doing?")[ [[What are you doing?->The Foreign Poem: What are you doing?]] ] [[Bid him farewell. (Each hero gains 1 XP.)->The Foreign Poem: Farewell]]You flip open a couple of pages and settle on a bit of verse. (text-style:"italic")[Then rose the King and moved his host by night And ever pushed Sir Mordred, league by league, Back to the sunset bound of Lyonesse— A land of old upheaven from the abyss By fire, to sink into the abyss again; Where fragments of forgotten peoples dwelt, And the long mountains ended in a coast Of ever-shifting sand, and far away The phantom circle of a moaning sea.] (text-size:0.75)[(text-style:"subscript")[Alfred, Lord Tennyson, “The Passing of Arthur,” Idylls of the King]] (unless: (history:) contains "The Foreign Poem: What are you doing?")[ [[What are you doing?->The Foreign Poem: What are you doing?]] ] [[Bid him farewell. (Each hero gains 1 XP.)->The Foreign Poem: Farewell]]You thank the stranger for his time and bid him farewell. (text-colour:cyan)[Each hero gains 1 XP.] [[End your turn.->Main]](set: $xp to it + 1)//''The Twisted Arena''// <div class="art art-arena"></div> Just across the way, not a hundred yards off, you hear a swelling chorus of voices. You tread carefully, picking your way across the rocky landscape to get a closer look without attracting anyone's attention. There, in the hollowed-out carcass of a giant beast, you see a large gathering of people of varied races chanting raucously as two pit fighters circle each other. Pennons and banners snap wildly as adjutants wave them furiously. An announcer calls above the din, frantically narrating the bout: "In this corner, the mighty and esteemed Sterric Jones battles for his life! He has been victorious thus far, but will he survive against our newest challenger?" You think to beat a hasty retreat, not liking the vibe of this place. But suddenly, a hand clamps on your shoulder. "Hello, friend. Or should I say, Trader? Come join us in the Twisted Arena. We seek new participants." Suddenly, robed figures emerge from all around you, and a chill runs through your bones. The strange insignia stitched into their sleeves gives them away. One of them smiles at you. "Don't try anything stupid," he says. "I can as easily slice your mind in two as breathe. Our master needs entertainment, so come fight in the arena." [[Trick them. (Hard Savoir faire check. On a failure, you fight in the arena.)->The Twisted Arena: Trick roll]] [[Attack them. (Medium Power check. Win or lose the roll, you fight their leader.)->The Twisted Arena: Attack roll]] [[Fight in the arena. (Draw 3 cards from the Deadlands enemy deck.)->The Twisted Arena: The arena]]Roll Savoir faire (Hard, 5 or higher), then pick your result. (dropdown: bind $rollText, "Choose...", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6") (link-repeat: "Submit roll")[ (if: $rollText is "5" or $rollText is "6")[(go-to: "The Twisted Arena: Trick succeeded")] (else-if: $rollText is "1" or $rollText is "2" or $rollText is "3" or $rollText is "4")[(go-to: "The Twisted Arena: Trick failed")] (else:)[Please choose a number first.] ]There's just something about that smarmy look on the robed man's face that makes you want to wipe it away. The problem, of course, is that you are vastly outnumbered. You sigh, racking your brain for a solution before you are thrown into the pit and left to who knows what fate. Finally, you acquiesce to their demands and head dejectedly into the arena. Just as you set foot into the bloodied sands, sullied by a previous combat, a thought occurs to you. "Have you come for spectacle?" you roar. The crowd erupts into a frenzy, eager to sate their bloodlust. "Today, your rogue masters have agreed to fight me." You gesture at the men, whose smiling faces have suddenly gone cold. They know that an overwhelming advantage in numbers would look poor to their audience. "You've sealed your fate, Trader," says the man, shaking his head, but he gestures for some of his compatriots to leave. (text-colour:purple)[Search the Deadlands enemy deck for a Mindscythe Acolyte and a Mindscythe Adept, and enter combat.] (text-colour:lime)[Select the outcome of your fight:] [[You won the fight.->The Twisted Arena: Trick fight won]] [[You were defeated.->The Twisted Arena: Arena lost]]There's just something about that smarmy look on the robed man's face that makes you want to wipe it away. The problem, of course, is that you are vastly outnumbered. You sigh, racking your brain for a solution before you are thrown into the pit and left to who knows what fate. Finally, you acquiesce to their demands and head dejectedly into the arena, thinking of nothing that can rescue you from your predicament. [[To the arena.->The Twisted Arena: The arena]]Roll Power (Medium, 4 or higher), then pick your result. (dropdown: bind $rollText, "Choose...", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6") (link-repeat: "Submit roll")[ (if: $rollText is "4" or $rollText is "5" or $rollText is "6")[(go-to: "The Twisted Arena: Attack succeeded")] (else-if: $rollText is "1" or $rollText is "2" or $rollText is "3")[(go-to: "The Twisted Arena: Attack failed")] (else:)[Please choose a number first.] ]"Is that what you think?" you ask the man. "I do," he replies, but whatever he says next is cut off as you abruptly lunge for him. He waves his hands in an attempt to ward you off, but you strike him down before he can get any further. Quickly, your compatriots lay waste to the robed men, much to their astonishment. But the smiling man seems more resilient. He rises from the dust, glowing with power: "You have made your last mistake, mortal." (text-colour:purple)[Search the Deadlands elite deck for the Mindscythe Master and enter combat. It starts the fight with half its printed WP.] (if: $heroes is 4)[(text-colour:purple)[Four heroes: also draw 1 enemy from the Deadlands enemy deck. It fights beside the elite, acts after it, and pays its printed drop.] ] (text-colour:lime)[Select the outcome of your fight:] [[You won the fight.->The Twisted Arena: Master fight won]] [[You were defeated.->The Twisted Arena: Master fight lost]]Whatever you thought you would accomplish, you were wrong. You launch a surprise attack, but it goes nowhere. He effortlessly circumvents your attack. "Foolish mortals," says the man, glowing with power, "your time living on this earth is done." (text-colour:purple)[Search the Deadlands elite deck for the Mindscythe Master and enter combat.] (if: $heroes is 4)[(text-colour:purple)[Four heroes: also draw 1 enemy from the Deadlands enemy deck. It fights beside the elite, acts after it, and pays its printed drop.] ] (text-colour:lime)[Select the outcome of your fight:] [[You won the fight.->The Twisted Arena: Master fight won]] [[You were defeated.->The Twisted Arena: Master fight lost]]You are shoved out onto the bloodstained sand to the roar of the crowd. Across the pit, the gates grind open, and your opponents come snarling out to meet you. (text-colour:purple)[Draw 3 cards from the Deadlands enemy deck and enter combat.] (text-colour:lime)[Select the outcome of your fight:] [[You won the fight.->The Twisted Arena: Arena won]] [[You were defeated.->The Twisted Arena: Arena lost]]When the last of your foes collapses into the sand, the arena falls silent for a moment before the crowd erupts. Coins and flowers rain down onto the sand, along with at least one boot, and the announcer screams himself hoarse inventing titles for you faster than you can hear them. The robed figures applaud as well, slowly, from the shadows. "Our master is entertained," one of them says. "Take your prize, Trader, and go, before he decides he wants to see you fight again." As the crowd stamps and howls for the next bout, you look up at the faces in the stands and realize that they are ordinary farmers and merchants, the same sort of people you might pass on any road. (text-colour:cyan)[Collect the fight's usual rewards.] (text-colour:yellow)[Each hero gains 3 gold.] (text-colour:green)[Draw from the top of the equipment deck until you reveal a Tier III card. Keep it, and put the other cards you revealed on the bottom of the deck.] [[Speak to the crowd. (Hard Wisdom check)->The Twisted Arena: Speak roll]] [[Take your winnings and go. (End your turn.)->Heroes fell]](set: $gold to it + 3 * $heroes)You fall to the sand, and the roar of the crowd fades to a dull ringing in your ears. When you come to, you are lying in the cold outside the carcass with your coin purses noticeably lighter and your wounds bandaged poorly by someone who didn't much care. Through the great ribs of the dead beast, you can hear the announcer working the crowd into a fresh frenzy for the next poor soul to step onto the sand. (text-colour:orange)[This defeat does not end your run. Every hero gets back up with 25% of their max WP. Fallen heroes still add Doom as usual.] (text-colour:yellow)[Each hero loses 3 gold.] [[End your turn.->Heroes fell]](set: $gold to (max: 0, it - 3 * $heroes))When the two robed men fall, the crowd goes wild, delighted by a fight they never expected to see. The rest of the Mindscythe melt into the shadows rather than face the jeers, and the announcer, who knows a good story when he sees one, presses a fat purse into your hands. "That was for the show," he says. "Do come back any time." (text-colour:cyan)[Collect the fight's usual rewards.] (text-colour:yellow)[Each hero gains 2 gold.] (text-colour:green)[Draw from the top of the equipment deck until you reveal a Tier II card. Keep it, and put the other cards you revealed on the bottom of the deck.] [[End your turn.->Heroes fell]](set: $gold to it + 2 * $heroes)The Master's glow gutters out, and he crumples into the dust, robes and all. Whatever hold he had over the arena dies with him: the pit fighters drop their weapons and the spectators hurry away, and before long you have the arena to yourselves. (text-colour:cyan)[Collect the elite's printed rewards.] [[End your turn.->Heroes fell]]The last thing you feel is a cold pressure closing around your thoughts, and you remember nothing more until you wake in the dust outside the arena with a pounding headache. It seems the Master has decided that you are more entertaining alive than dead. (text-colour:orange)[This defeat does not end your run. Every hero gets back up with 25% of their max WP. Fallen heroes still add Doom as usual.] [[End your turn.->Heroes fell]]Roll Wisdom (Hard, 5 or higher), then pick your result. (dropdown: bind $rollText, "Choose...", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6") (link-repeat: "Submit roll")[ (if: $rollText is "5" or $rollText is "6")[(go-to: "The Twisted Arena: Crowd convinced")] (else-if: $rollText is "1" or $rollText is "2" or $rollText is "3" or $rollText is "4")[(go-to: "The Twisted Arena: Crowd unmoved")] (else:)[Please choose a number first.] ]You climb onto the great ribs of the carcass and raise your hands, and to your surprise, the crowd quiets. "Hear me. Are Traders not justly lauded the world over?" you say. The crowd shouts its agreement. "Then I say this, and I say it once: to partake in the spilling of blood for enjoyment's sake is not an act of courage. The only noble violence is that in defense of something fragile, and only as a last resort. "To revel in the bloodshed of others is a coward's way, is it not? But we are brave, are we not? We are warriors. "I say, if Traders are lauded the world over, render me the respect I am due. Have I not earned it? Have I not earned the glory of the battlefield? I say: if I have, go not the child's way any longer. I ask you one final time: are we cowards or are we warriors?" Nobody answers. One by one, and then in clumps, the spectators begin to leave. By the time the robed figures realize what is happening, the stands are half empty. The announcer finds you at the edge of the camp, hoarse, his bright coat gone dusty. "They'll have my head for this," he says cheerfully. "Best day of my life. Mind if I come along? You could use someone to tell people how good you are." (set: $supported to true, $arenaSupport to true) (text-colour:orange)[Your party is now Supported: the announcer joins your caravan.] (text-colour:orange)[Arena Announcer Support: every subsequent fight pays your party a flat 2 extra gold.] [[End your turn.->Heroes fell]]You climb onto the great ribs of the carcass and raise your hands, and the crowd quiets for all of a few seconds before someone throws a turnip at you. A great deal of other produce follows it, and you retreat under a hail of vegetables and boos while the delighted announcer christens you "the Preacher of the Pit." [[End your turn.->Heroes fell]]//''Strength Competition''// <div class="art art-strength"></div> You make port at one of the many fishing villages that dot the Azure Coast, looking to rest and resupply. There in the town square, you hear a din and come upon a scene: a burly man flexes shamelessly, his muscles rippling across his shirtless torso. "He's the strongest man in the world!" says a short fellow, his hype man, obviously. "Does anyone dare challenge me to a battle of muscle?" says the beefy man, a wide grin with perfect white teeth splitting his face. He looks around. "Anyone? Anyone who thinks they can best me will be rewarded handsomely," he says. [[Sure. (You make up to three Power rolls.)->Strength Competition: Betty]] [[Nah. (End your turn.)->Main]]You step forward. The strongman looks you up and down. "A challenger approaches! Let's see if they can handle our first task." The hype man leads out a sickly-looking cow. "Old Betty here," says the strongman, "doesn't like to be milked. Let's see who can milk her best." "Uhhhh," says Rudolph, but you silence him. The strongman demonstrates milking her udders with ease and then invites you to try. You do so without problem. "But that's not the challenge," says the strongman. "You must milk her with only your pinky finger." Again, he demonstrates successfully. Betty moos plaintively. "This is weird," whispers Thistle. Roll Power (Easy, 3 or higher), then pick your result. (dropdown: bind $rollText, "Choose...", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6") (link-repeat: "Submit roll")[ (if: $rollText is "3" or $rollText is "4" or $rollText is "5" or $rollText is "6")[(go-to: "Strength Competition: The hay")] (else-if: $rollText is "1" or $rollText is "2")[(go-to: "Strength Competition: Betty failed")] (else:)[Please choose a number first.] ]"Ha," says the strongman. "'Twas but a trifling task. A warm-up, if you will. A beginning. A start." "An entrée," adds the hype man. "A genesis. An //inception//. The onset of something."
