"What in tarnation is going on?" says Rudolph. (text-colour:green)[You win a Potion of Healing. Take one from the potion deck.] "Anyways," declares the strongman, "our next task: baling hay." The crowd oohs and aahs as he leads you to a barn where there are a LOT of hay bales that need to be stacked. You begin to wonder if you are just being tricked into doing farm work. Roll Power (Medium, 4 or higher), then pick your result. (dropdown: bind $rollText, "Choose...", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6") (link-repeat: "Submit roll")[ (if: $rollText is "4" or $rollText is "5" or $rollText is "6")[(go-to: "Strength Competition: The stone")] (else-if: $rollText is "1" or $rollText is "2" or $rollText is "3")[(go-to: "Strength Competition: Hay failed")] (else:)[Please choose a number first.] ]Several hours later, you are done, drenched in sweat, scratched, itchy, dusty, and sneezing. You stare around you in disbelief as the crowd is still there, watching. "Don't these people have anything better to do?" you muse. "No," says a bystander. (text-colour:yellow)[The crowd tosses coins for your trouble. Each hero gains 2 gold.] "For our final task," announces the hype man, "if you all will follow me." You arrive at the scene where a gleaming weapon is buried in stone. "Aha!" says the strongman. "Now we arrive at the greatest test of your strength. Draw this nondescript weapon from the stone that has been here for at least three centuries and receive the blessing of kings. Also, you will be named ruler of all these lands." "I feel like things have escalated," says Thistle quietly. "Yeah, just a few hours ago you were milking a cow. Now you're about to become royalty," Rudolph says dazedly to you. The hype man whispers in the strongman's ear. "Ah," says the strongman, "the clause about becoming royalty has since expired. But you'll get a shiny new weapon." "Can you even take this weapon out of the stone?" you ask. "Of course," says the man. "I'm the strongest man in the world, but I'd like to see you try." Roll Power (Hard, 5 or higher), then pick your result. (dropdown: bind $rollText, "Choose...", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6") (link-repeat: "Submit roll")[ (if: $rollText is "5" or $rollText is "6")[(go-to: "Strength Competition: Victory")] (else-if: $rollText is "1" or $rollText is "2" or $rollText is "3" or $rollText is "4")[(go-to: "Strength Competition: Stone failed")] (else:)[Please choose a number first.] ](set: $gold to it + 2 * $heroes)You heave with all your might, and the weapon comes free. "Incredible," declares the strongman. "Amazing," says the hype man. "Astounding," says the strongman. "Inconceivable," says the hype man. "Truly," says the strongman, "you deserve the title of strongest man and/or woman in the world. I am in awe of your handsome muscles and beautiful physique. We shall spread your name far and wide, to every passing ship." "Yeah," says the hype man. "Consider me your new personal hype man." (set: $renowned to true) (text-colour:green)[Draw from the top of the equipment deck until you reveal a weapon. Keep it, and put the other cards you revealed on the bottom of the deck.] (text-colour:orange)[You are now Renowned. Some events offer Renowned heroes special choices.] ''Renown.'' Choose one benefit for the rest of this run: * Your first Rest in each town is free. * At the start of each fight, the first enemy drawn is Weak 1. * Choose one of your moves: each of its ATK steps deals +3 damage. [[End your turn.->Main]]"I... I think she's out of milk," you protest, as not a single drop squeezes out despite your best efforts. The strongman shakes his head at you. "Tsk, tsk, tsk," he says. "Betty never runs out of milk. You are not a worthy challenger. Begone from my sight!" "Begone!" repeats the hype man. "Begone, be gone, be gone!" "All right," says Rudolph. "I think I'm done with this place." [[End your turn.->Main]]Eventually, your arms give out, burning, and you set down the bale. You are sweating, itchy all over from straw dust, and have a dozen tiny scratches on your skin from the pokey straw. "Giving up so easily?" asks the straw man—er, strongman. This work is messing with your head. You bow out. "Boss just got tricked into unpaid labor," says Thistle. "They were coerced by the wiles of a good strength scheme. You've got to learn to spot them when you're young, otherwise you get seduced by your own ego. I myself have never fallen prey to such an easy trap," says Rudolph. You stare at both of them. "Let's go," you say sourly. [[End your turn.->Main]]You heave with all your might, but the weapon does not come free. You step away from the weapon, panting. Suddenly, the strongman is joining you, and together you break the weapon free. "Listen, friend," he whispers. "Thanks for helping me do those chores. I really didn't want to do them by myself. Everybody thinks because I've got these amazing muscles that I should work like an ox. It really isn't fair sometimes, you know." He clasps your hand. "You're a good one, Trader. Take this weapon as thanks." (text-colour:green)[Draw from the top of the equipment deck until you reveal a weapon. Keep it, and put the other cards you revealed on the bottom of the deck.] [[End your turn.->Main]]//''A Murder Secret''// <div class="art art-murder"></div> At a crossroads, a man sits on a log, novel in one hand, the other hand resting his chin. As you approach, he harrumphs, snaps the book shut, and loudly proclaims, "Gol-darn it!" "What's the matter?" you ask. "They shouldn't be called mystery books," he declares, in a bit of a non sequitur. "Is that what you're reading?" you ask. "Yes, a murder mystery. Here's my spiel: it should be called “a murder secret.” "No, I get that it doesn't have alliteration, but hold on, hear me out. Do you know why a murder mystery is never satisfying? I mean, it can be kind of satisfying, but do you know why it's not really satisfying?" [[Uhhhhhh...->A Murder Secret: A divine experience]] [[We don't have time for this.->A Murder Secret: Slip away]]"A mystery is a divine experience. The unfolding layers of the onion draw you to some higher truth, some new awakening and enlightenment. "A secret is just that: a bit of information that you don't have until you do." [[But what does this have to do with mystery novels?->A Murder Secret: Being good]] [[Bail out of the conversation.->A Murder Secret: Slip away]]"Well, it's just that," says the man, "there's no mystery to human nature doing some sort of evil. That's the same tired, played-out trope we've seen over and over again. "You know what is a real mystery? Being good. "Think about it. When you think of the great evil men or women of the world (the despotic rulers, the tyrants, the cruel and deranged psychopaths), there's no great insight there. You can pick at them, prod at them, and pick apart their motivations as you would dissect an insect, but it is always in some kind of lurid fascination or a fact-finding mission to figure out how such a reprehensible figure of society was produced, and how we can avoid having such reprehensible figures of society in the future. "Now think of the good." [[Try to interject.->A Murder Secret: The mystery solved]] [[Quietly sneak away.->A Murder Secret: Slip away]]You open your mouth to speak, but the man keeps going. "The good people of the world, the saints, those who have sacrificed more than what we can humanly conceive of sacrificing: they are the real mystery. In them we ponder, we wonder, and we are open to new possibilities, new avenues of thought and learning, a deepening of our consciousness, of our ability to cognize new thoughts, to feel for others, to overcome. "The tales that stick in the mind are not those of the most evil or depraved, but of the most heroic. They are the mystery solved. And so I say fie to yet another bargain-bin murder mystery." He slams the book down on the ground and harrumphs once more. "Truly, enlighten me. O universe, reveal your divine mystery to me," he says, raising his hands up to the sky. Then he looks at you. "Oh, sorry, didn't notice you there." You feel wiser, but you don't know if it's from what he said or the patience, the growth in patience, it took for you to listen. (text-colour:orange)[You gain +1 Wisdom for the rest of this run.] [[End your turn.->Main]]You back away slowly, and the man doesn't appear to notice. He is still talking when you round the bend in the road, and if the wind is right, you can hear him for some time after that. [[End your turn.->Main]]//''Unsettling Certainty''// <div class="art art-unsettling"></div> Thunder rumbles in the sky, and you feel a sickening certainty that something is awry. It is subtle, but the mind is perceptive: slight changes in air pressure, in temperature, in what body language is saying, in the very breeze. The breath of the world speaks to you, and you feel yourself naturally tensing, as if waiting for something to happen. (link: "Steel yourself.")[(if: $doom >= 5)[(go-to: "Unsettling Certainty: High Doom")](else:)[(go-to: "Unsettling Certainty: Low Doom")]]As a Trader, you have no time for fear, but you must acknowledge facts. There is a sinister force lingering in this world that must be dealt with, and the time for conflict with it is fast approaching. You reckon you will soon have to deal with it, or at least finish your quest before it arrives. (text-colour:magenta)[Doom +3.] (text-colour:cyan)[Each hero gains 5 XP.] [[End your turn.->Main]](set: $doom to it + 3, $xp to it + 5)As if on cue, your journey takes you to a cavern. Inside, there is a harbinger of a foe to come, not quite at their strength, but close enough. [[Root this evil out from the world. (Draw a card from the elite deck of the section you are in and fight it.)->Unsettling Certainty: Root it out]] [[Leave, plan, and train more to gain enough strength to deal with it. (End your turn.)->Main]]Roll Savoir faire (Hard, 5 or higher), then pick your result. (dropdown: bind $rollText, "Choose...", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6") (link-repeat: "Submit roll")[ (if: $rollText is "5" or $rollText is "6")[(go-to: "Burning Home: Rescue")] (else-if: $rollText is "1" or $rollText is "2" or $rollText is "3" or $rollText is "4")[(go-to: "Burning Home: Driven back")] (else:)[Please choose a number first.] ]In a blink, you have leapt into action, grabbing a cloak and dousing it with water, and grabbing a young man with the thickest clothes. "Twelve seconds," you say to him, then grab his hand. He nods with a fierce determination. After taking a lungful of air, you burst through the front door, hand in hand, counting silently in your head. Within the span of those heartbeats, both of you have searched every room. You pass strange burning lumps until, at last, your compatriot finds a teenage girl, perhaps sixteen or seventeen, lying on the floor in terror. Together, you get her up, wrap her in a sopping cloak, and rush her as quickly as possible, practically carrying her through the front door and out into the clearing. The townsfolk swarm around both of you, attending to you. Your lungs feel like they're on fire, and some of your skin is singed, but you are alive and will recover. It takes time to heal. The townsfolk set you up in their healer's abode, a simple stone building on the outskirts of town, where a frogfolk woman (uncommon in these parts) carefully measures herbs and distills them into potions. She smiles at you as much as a frogfolk can smile when she notices you've awakened from your rest. "You have a strong constitution," she croaks. "Here, take this." [[Continue->Burning Home: Recovery]]The liquid is surprisingly minty and refreshing. It feels cold as it seemingly grips your lungs, and then the pain that was inside them subsides. "The girl?" you croak back. Your voice sounds scratchy to your ears. "As healthy as a tadpole," says the woman, laughing the strange laugh of her kind. She makes a sign, some sort of religious symbol, towards a small window placed near the top of your hut where the sunlight shines through, and you recall that frogfolk find spiritual comfort in the presence of the sun. Soon, the elderly man from before comes in and shakes your hand. "My name is Richter," he says, "and what you and my grandson did was a brave thing. We are all honored by your presence and indebted to you. I have often wondered if what they say about Traders is true. Today, you have proven that you are worthy of all the tales. "We have little in the way of coin to give you, but we will honor your name. And please have this keepsake. And perhaps Tisha here can donate some of her healing herbs." (text-colour:red)[Each hero heals 3 WP.] (text-colour:cyan)[Each hero gains 2 XP.] (text-colour:green)[Gain 2 Herbs and 1 Exotic Goods.] [[Wait, there's something else...->Burning Home: Something else]] [[It's time to go. Thank the man and take your leave.->Main]](set: $xp to it + 2, $herbs to it + 2, $exotic to it + 1)Something tickles your mind, and it takes you a moment to recall it. Your subconscious processes what your conscious mind could not. The burning building had windows, and within those rooms were lumps. Lumps of burning dung, you realize, matching the smell when you came in. "Did someone set the blaze?" you ask Richter. He grimaces. "I'm afraid so, or so we have gathered. We believe it was a farmhand, a young lad who was rebuffed by the girl." [[Ask if you can question the farmhand.->Burning Home: Balfour]] [[Tell him you're glad justice is being served, and bid him farewell.->Main]](if: visits is 1)[He seems to hesitate, but then accedes to your request. He leads you from the healer's hut back to the town square, where an uncertain-looking young man is bound and stood on a platform. It seems as though the entire town is there, many with frightful looks on their faces, threatening woe upon the young man. Richter pushes through. "Hear me, townsfolk. The hero Trader who saved Rebecca wishes to speak with Balfour. I know you all seek justice, but we should allow them that. It is their due." The townsfolk reluctantly agree, several of them bemoaning the delay in justice. Balfour is a slight youth with tousled dark hair, wearing rough-spun clothing. He has calloused hands and wrings them nervously. You notice he stinks of dung.](else:)[Balfour waits on the platform, wringing his hands. The crowd mutters.] (if: $balfourSilent is true)[Balfour stares at his feet. He will not say another word.](else:)[What do you ask him? (unless: (history:) contains "Burning Home: Where were you")[[[Where were you when the fire started?->Burning Home: Where were you]] ](unless: (history:) contains "Burning Home: Why you")[[[Why do they think it was you?->Burning Home: Why you]] ](if: (history:) contains "Burning Home: Why you" and (history:) does not contain "Burning Home: Hands")[[[Show me your hands.->Burning Home: Hands]] ](if: (history:) contains "Burning Home: Why you" and (history:) does not contain "Burning Home: Dung")[[[Can dung even burn?->Burning Home: Dung]] ][[Admit it. You did it because she turned you down.->Burning Home: Spite]]] ''Or make your judgment:'' [[Declare him guilty.->Burning Home: Guilty]] [[Declare him innocent.->Burning Home: Innocent]]"I was mucking out Pell's stable on the far side of the hamlet, same as every morning, and nobody saw me there except the horses. When the bell rang, I ran, and I got there just as she screamed. I tried to go in after her, but Wendel's boys held me back, and then you went in instead." [[Ask him something else.->Burning Home: Balfour]] [[Declare him guilty.->Burning Home: Guilty]] [[Declare him innocent.->Burning Home: Innocent]]"Because I stink of dung, I guess, and so did the fire." He swallows. "And because Rebecca turned me down in front of everyone yesterday. And I said some things I shouldn't have. Bad things." He looks like he will be sick. [[Ask him something else.->Burning Home: Balfour]] [[Declare him guilty.->Burning Home: Guilty]] [[Declare him innocent.->Burning Home: Innocent]](if: (history:) contains "Burning Home: Dung")[(set: $balfourCleared to true)]He holds them out. They are calloused and cracked, with dirt ground deep into the creases, but there are no blisters or burns. [[Ask him something else.->Burning Home: Balfour]] [[Declare him guilty.->Burning Home: Guilty]] [[Declare him innocent.->Burning Home: Innocent]](if: (history:) contains "Burning Home: Hands")[(set: $balfourCleared to true)]"Oh, yeah," he says, brightening up, as if happy you asked him an easy question. "I mean, fresh it won't. You want dung cakes, packed and dried in the sun for a whole season. You do that, it burns real good." Suddenly he frowns. "Why do you ask?" [[Ask him something else.->Burning Home: Balfour]] [[Declare him guilty.->Burning Home: Guilty]] [[Declare him innocent.->Burning Home: Innocent]](set: $balfourSilent to true)Balfour's face hardens. "I've said all I'm going to say," he tells you, and somewhere in the crowd, a man cheers. [[Declare him guilty.->Burning Home: Guilty]] [[Declare him innocent.->Burning Home: Innocent]](if: $balfourCleared is true)[(go-to: "Burning Home: Freed")](else:)[(go-to: "Burning Home: Not convinced")]"He did it," you say. The crowd roars its approval, and Balfour doesn't resist as they drag him down from the platform, though he looks back at you once over their heads before he disappears from view. Richter claps you on the shoulder. "Justice has been done," he says. The smell of smoke follows you out of the hamlet, and for a long way down the road, you find yourself hoping that you made the right call. [[End your turn.->Main]]"He didn't do it," you say. The crowd goes quiet. Then someone laughs. "On whose word? He stinks like the fire, he had his reasons, and you've got nothing but a feeling." You open your mouth, and find you have nothing to say. Richter shakes his head sadly. "All the evidence points to him, Trader." They lead Balfour off toward the stocks. You leave the hamlet certain you were right, and certain it didn't matter. [[End your turn.->Main]]"He didn't do it," you say, "and I can prove it," and the crowd quiets down to listen. "That fire was set with dung cakes. Fresh muck won't burn, and cakes take a whole season to dry, but Rebecca only turned him down yesterday. Whoever did this was planning it long before she broke his heart." You hold up Balfour's hands for all to see. "And whoever set a burning cake in every window of that house would have scorched fingers. Look at his: there isn't a mark on them." A murmur ripples through the crowd. Richter studies Balfour's hands for some time before he draws his knife and cuts the ropes. Balfour rubs his wrists and thanks you quietly, then leans close. "There's something I didn't tell them, because they'd have laughed at me. I've seen it twice now, last night outside that townhouse and once before out in the fields. It's pale as bone, with no face, and it moves like smoke drifting over water." "The White Bandit," whispers a woman in the crowd, who then looks embarrassed for having said it. "Everyone says it's a story for children," says Balfour, "but I followed it, and I know where it goes." (set: $bandit_location to true)(text-colour:cyan)[Each hero gains 2 XP.] (text-colour:orange)[You know where the White Bandit goes. You may cross its path again.] [[End your turn.->Main]](set: $xp to it + 2)You join the line of villagers passing buckets hand to hand from the well. Two of the young men disappear into the smoke, and after a minute that feels much longer, they stagger back out carrying a coughing, soot-covered girl between them. A cheer goes up along the line when it becomes clear that she is going to be all right. By the time the fire is out, the townhouse is a blackened shell and you are soaked to the knees, and the elderly man comes over to shake your hand. (text-colour:cyan)[Each hero gains 1 XP.] [[End your turn.->Main]](set: $xp to it + 1)In a blink, you have leapt into action. You burst through the front door. You pass strange burning lumps until, at last, you find a teenage girl, perhaps sixteen or seventeen, lying on the floor in terror. You get her up, wrapping her in your cloak, and rush her as quickly as possible, practically carrying her through the front door and out into the clearing. She seems fine, but you collapse, burned and exhausted. (set: $scarred to true)(text-colour:cyan)[Each hero gains 2 XP.] (text-colour:orange)[You have gained the Scarred tag.] (text-colour:red)[You lose 4 max WP.] [[End your turn.->Main]](set: $xp to it + 2)//''A Fine to Pay''// <div class="art art-fine"></div> You round a bend in the road and find a man standing in the middle of it, as if he has been waiting for you specifically. The wind is tousling his matted hair. His fingers are clenching and unclenching in a hypnotic pattern. The man has captivated your attention such that you realize belatedly he is standing next to a fallen cart. A horse lies on its side, whinnying in distress. Quite suddenly, you find your hand clenching and unclenching too, and drifting towards a weapon. "Hold there, stranger," says the man. He has a curious sort of accent, clipping his words short, as if he were cutting them off at the end with a knife. "I am no stranger, but a Trader," you reply, gesturing to your caravan without taking your eyes off him. "A merchant who seeks to pass unmolested." "And so you shall," he replies. "But first, you must pay a fine." [[What do you propose?->A Fine to Pay: Propose]] [[I think not.->A Fine to Pay: I think not]]He draws out a long scythe, as if to harvest grain. "It is not gold I wish from you, but wits. My fine is that you challenge my intellect, for I perceive that none can. Should you successfully do so, I shall reward you. And should you fail, I will reap what is mine." [[Continue->A Fine to Pay: Battle of Wits]]"Yeah, I don't think so," you say. "We have done you no wrong, and you have no hold over these lands or over us. To impinge upon our free will is a crime. We owe you no fine, and we will pay no such thing." The man licks his lips and seems to be considering your words. He raises a hand to his unshaven face. Finally, he draws out a long scythe, as if to harvest grain. "It is not gold I wish from you, but wits. My fine is that you challenge my intellect, for I perceive that none can. Should you successfully do so, I shall reward you. And should you fail, I will reap what is mine." [[Very well, test us then.->A Fine to Pay: Battle of Wits]] [[Intellect, shmintellect. Rush the man, weapons drawn. (Hard Power check)->A Fine to Pay: Rush]] [[Refuse him.->A Fine to Pay: Refuse]]"Nope," you say, "not gonna do that. We are gonna move on, and you're gonna leave us alone. That's my final word." You declare your words with such certainty that the man seems taken aback. "Well..." he begins, but you talk over him. "Absolutely not," you say to whatever he was about to spout. "Goodbye." You motion your caravan forward and you all proceed. For whatever reason, the tension is gone. The man seems to recognize that he lost whatever hold he had over you; whether he is puzzled, dissatisfied, or pleased, you cannot tell. (text-colour:magenta)[Doom −1.] [[End your turn.->Main]](set: $doom to (max: 0, it - 1))Roll Power (Hard, 5 or higher), then pick your result. (dropdown: bind $rollText, "Choose...", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6") (link-repeat: "Submit roll")[ (if: $rollText is "5" or $rollText is "6")[(go-to: "A Fine to Pay: Rush won")] (else-if: $rollText is "1" or $rollText is "2" or $rollText is "3" or $rollText is "4")[(go-to: "A Fine to Pay: Rush failed")] (else:)[Please choose a number first.] ]You charge forward at the man, and he seems shocked at your speed. With one precise strike, you slice the haft of his scythe in two, rendering the fearsome-looking implement impotent. "You dare," the man begins, but you slap him. He seems utterly stupefied by the boldness of your aggression, and frankly, a little embarrassed. "Please excuse us," you say. You motion the caravan forward, and he allows you to pass without further incident. (text-colour:magenta)[Doom −1.] (text-colour:cyan)[Each hero gains 2 XP.] [[End your turn.->Main]](set: $doom to (max: 0, it - 1), $xp to it + 2)You charge forward at the man, but you are too slow. He lazily reacts, taking the butt of his scythe and jabbing it into your chin. You reel back in pain. "You may not pass without paying the fine," he says, a little more firmly. "Come, let us test your wits." (text-colour:red)[You lose 11 WP.] [[Continue->A Fine to Pay: Battle of Wits]]"Each of you was given a field that you did not plant and cannot sell," he says. "You reap it whether you wish to or not, and when the last row is cut, it is done with you. What is it?" [[Wheat.->A Fine to Pay: Wrong]] [[Your sorrows.->A Fine to Pay: Wrong]] [[Death.->A Fine to Pay: Wrong]] [[Your days.->A Fine to Pay: Right]]"No," he says, and the scythe moves. You scramble wildly out of the way, but it isn't aimed at you. It passes through the side of your wagon as if the boards were smoke, and when it comes back, the blade is heavy with your stores. He tips them into a sack you did not see him holding, ties it off, and steps aside. "Fine paid," he says. "Mind the horse." As you pass by the fallen horse, you cannot help but wonder what became of its previous rider. (text-colour:green)[Each hero loses 2 Food.] (text-colour:magenta)[Doom +1.] [[End your turn.->Main]](set: $food to (max: 0, it - 2 * $heroes), $doom to it + 1)The man says nothing for a while, and then he laughs, a short, clipped laugh like everything else about him. "Days," he repeats. "Most say death, but death is only the man holding the scythe." He looks down at his own scythe as if noticing it for the first time. He walks to the fallen horse and cuts the traces with one stroke, and once the animal has scrambled to its feet, he swings onto its back and rides off down the road you came from, leaving the cart where it lies with all of its cargo still aboard. [[End your turn.->Main]]Your hand closes on something small and warm. When you look up, the pile is gone. So is he. Only the door, flat on the floor, says anyone was here at all. (text-colour:green)[Draw from the top of the equipment deck until you reveal a Tier II card. Keep it, and put the other cards you revealed on the bottom of the deck.] (text-colour:magenta)[Doom +1.] [[End your turn.->Main]](set: $doom to it + 1)He tilts his head, as if the question is a coin he's checking for bite marks. "A thief takes what isn't missed," he says. "I take what isn't seen." Then the room is only a room. Downstairs, the kiplings are already shouting about their lost income. (text-colour:cyan)[Each hero gains 2 XP.] [[End your turn.->Main]](set: $xp to it + 2)You lift the door back into its frame as best you can. It doesn't fit anymore. Neither, you suspect, will the memory. [[End your turn.->Main]]//''As Big as My Palm''// <div class="art art-rumors"></div> Today it is raining, the dark sky shadowing the land and peppering the cobblestone streets of a small city with tiny, pinprick-sized rain droplets. Something about the jewel that old man was muttering about nags at you. You turn to your left and notice a hole-in-the-wall tavern whose door you hadn't seen before. You step inside to escape the drizzle and are met by a sea of surly-faced sailors. You press forward, unintimidated, as a Trader must be, and sit down at the bar, where the bartender grabs a glass and places it in front of you. "What'll it be to drink?" he asks you. [[Treasure.->Palm: Treasure]] [[A milkshake.->Palm: Shoved out]] [[Something fizzy and carbonated.->Palm: Shoved out]]"We ain't got that here," says the bartender, and he shoves you out the door. [[Return to Diver's Key.->Diver's Key]]At the mention of treasure, the bartender's eyes widen fractionally, and he asks you a follow-up question: "What size drink would you like?" [[Massive.->Palm: Shoved out]] [[Huge.->Palm: Shoved out]] [[As big as my palm.->Palm: The prophesied one]]As if on cue, you notice a lot of eyes staring at you. "So you're the one," says the bartender. "I knew this day would come." He grabs a diamond the size of your palm from behind the bar and proffers it to you. It is stunning and gorgeous. You suddenly start to sweat, feeling as if you've stepped into something you don't quite understand. You realize belatedly that these men are not just sailors. You note the uniformity of their braided beards and the hungry look in their eyes. No, they're not just sailors, but Northmen. "You are the prophesied one," says the bartender. "Huh, what do you know? A foreign Trader. Well, anyways, good luck. The big bad boss will love facing you in combat, as is her right." Without a further word, he shoves the jewel into your hand and guides you out the door. Every player gains the same amount, and a win resets the count. ''Spending'' happens at setup, before the first map turn. Everything lasts that run only. Unspent LP carries over. <table class="lp-table" style="border-collapse:collapse;width:100%"><tr><th style="padding:3px 14px 3px 0;border-bottom:1px solid rgba(43,30,18,.18);text-align:left">Buy</th><th style="padding:3px 14px 3px 0;border-bottom:1px solid rgba(43,30,18,.18);text-align:left">LP</th></tr><tr><td style="padding:3px 14px 3px 0;border-bottom:1px solid rgba(43,30,18,.18);text-align:left">Potion of Healing or Potion of Iron</td><td style="padding:3px 14px 3px 0;border-bottom:1px solid rgba(43,30,18,.18);text-align:left">1</td></tr><tr><td style="padding:3px 14px 3px 0;border-bottom:1px solid rgba(43,30,18,.18);text-align:left">Draw 1 potion</td><td style="padding:3px 14px 3px 0;border-bottom:1px solid rgba(43,30,18,.18);text-align:left">2</td></tr><tr><td style="padding:3px 14px 3px 0;border-bottom:1px solid rgba(43,30,18,.18);text-align:left">+3 gold</td><td style="padding:3px 14px 3px 0;border-bottom:1px solid rgba(43,30,18,.18);text-align:left">2</td></tr><tr><td style="padding:3px 14px 3px 0;border-bottom:1px solid rgba(43,30,18,.18);text-align:left">Draw 1 Tier I weapon or armor</td><td style="padding:3px 14px 3px 0;border-bottom:1px solid rgba(43,30,18,.18);text-align:left">3</td></tr><tr><td style="padding:3px 14px 3px 0;border-bottom:1px solid rgba(43,30,18,.18);text-align:left">Draw 1 Tier II weapon or armor</td><td style="padding:3px 14px 3px 0;border-bottom:1px solid rgba(43,30,18,.18);text-align:left">6</td></tr><tr><td style="padding:3px 14px 3px 0;border-bottom:1px solid rgba(43,30,18,.18);text-align:left">Start at level 2</td><td style="padding:3px 14px 3px 0;border-bottom:1px solid rgba(43,30,18,.18);text-align:left">8</td></tr></table> Weapons and armor are always drawn at random. The usual one-weapon, one-armor limit applies. [[Back->Start]]The farmer listens, scratches his head, and looks from you to the sylvan and back again. "Well, I'll be," he says at last. "Three weeks, and the crows haven't touched my wheat." He presses a sack of turnips into your arms for your trouble. Behind him, the sylvan lowers his arms with a long, creaking sigh. "Thank... you," he says. (text-colour:green)[Gain 2 Food.] (text-colour:cyan)[Each hero gains 1 XP.] (text-colour:magenta)[Doom +1.] [[End your turn.->Main]](set: $food to it + 2, $xp to it + 1, $doom to it + 1)//''Eli's Crossing''// The long marble bridge of ancient construction that spans the waters of a gushing river, which pour into the azure sea, seems to shimmer in the morning light. The bridge is half again as wide as ten horses and perhaps ten times as long. "She would have come through here," muses Rudolph, and you nod absently. As a child, you used to dream of this place, and of seeing the world. Though it has only been two weeks since you left Hearthhome, it feels as if your previous life was in the distant past. You can only imagine what adventures your sister has already had. A sudden spike of fear invades your mind as you wonder what happened to her. Why haven't you heard anything? You feel an urgency to find her, as if a creeping doom were settling over the world, and only the resolution of your quest will stave it off. As if in tandem with your thoughts, something jumps to your attention: a carving somehow scratched into the marble itself, very faint. You see the letters K-A-I-R-O-S. Kairos: what could it mean? The rest of the day passes without incident while you ponder the message. Did it have any significance, or was it just the idle scratching of someone? Any person could have inscribed it into the stone with enough persistence. Surely it had nothing to do with Marla. Surely. "Boss," says Thistle, breaking your reverie. "Up ahead." You come upon the wreckage of what looks like a small village. Houses left in ruins. No people remain. It leaves an ominous feeling. It fights beside the elite, acts after it, and pays its printed drop.] ](text-colour:green)[If you win, collect the elite's printed rewards.] [[After the fight.->Heroes fell]]You leave the old man to his fishing and sail on, and the feeling of change stays with you long after his boat has disappeared behind you. (text-colour:orange)[Each hero raises one attribute of their choice (Power, Wisdom or Savoir faire) by 1 for the rest of this run.] [[End your turn.->Main]]You bait a hook and cast out where the old man's line was bobbing earlier. For a long while, nothing happens at all, until the line suddenly goes taut with a force that nearly pulls you into the sea. Roll Power (Medium, 4 or higher), then pick your result. (dropdown: bind $rollText, "Choose...", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6") (link-repeat: "Submit roll")[ (if: $rollText is "4" or $rollText is "5" or $rollText is "6")[(go-to: "Old Man: Fish 2")] (else-if: $rollText is "1" or $rollText is "2" or $rollText is "3")[(go-to: "Old Man: The fish got away")] (else:)[Please choose a number first.] ]You manage to hold on, and through the water, you catch a glimpse of gold. When the fish runs, you remember what the old man said about patience, so you let it run and wait for it to tire. Roll Wisdom (Medium, 4 or higher), then pick your result. (dropdown: bind $rollText, "Choose...", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6") (link-repeat: "Submit roll")[ (if: $rollText is "4" or $rollText is "5" or $rollText is "6")[(go-to: "Old Man: Fish 3")] (else-if: $rollText is "1" or $rollText is "2" or $rollText is "3")[(go-to: "Old Man: The fish got away")] (else:)[Please choose a number first.] ]At last, the fish tires and comes alongside the skiff. Up close, it is enormous, with scales as big as coins and a round eye that watches you calmly, and you will need a delicate touch to lift it out of the sea without hurting it. Roll Savoir faire (Medium, 4 or higher), then pick your result. (dropdown: bind $rollText, "Choose...", "1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6") (link-repeat: "Submit roll")[ (if: $rollText is "4" or $rollText is "5" or $rollText is "6")[(go-to: "Old Man: The golden fish")] (else-if: $rollText is "1" or $rollText is "2" or $rollText is "3")[(go-to: "Old Man: The fish got away")] (else:)[Please choose a number first.] ]You hold the golden fish just long enough to feel how cool and heavy it is before you lower it back into the sea, where it lingers beside the skiff for a moment before swimming away. Someone down the shore saw the whole thing, and by nightfall, half the coast has heard the story. (set: $renowned to true) (text-colour:orange)[You are now Renowned. Some events offer Renowned heroes special choices.] ''Renown.'' Choose one benefit for the rest of this run: * Your first Rest in each town is free. * At the start of each fight, the first enemy drawn is Weak 1. * Choose one of your moves: each of its ATK steps deals +3 damage. [[End your turn.->Main]]The line goes slack, and far out in the water, you see a flash of gold turn in the deep and disappear. You are left with an ordinary fish or two for the pot and a good story about the one that got away. (text-colour:cyan)[Each hero gains 1 XP.] (text-colour:green)[Each hero gains 1 Food.] [[End your turn.->Main]](set: $xp to it + 1, $food to it + $heroes)"I understand," you say. "It's not your battle to deal with, so to speak. I'm sorry if we have disturbed you." "No, it's okay," he says. "Look, it was just bad business, and I warned her not to go into the Deadlands, same as Martin. And as for the rest..." He shakes his head. "Well, something happened. I'm a sailor now, and I don't really believe in all the tall tales that the seafaring folk say. But look"—he knocks on wood—"this is just bad. Bad juju. Marla made her choice. I say leave the whole thing be." And at that, he leaves. [[Return to Port Pearl.->Port Pearl]]"Look, Marla, you guys hung out a lot, right? I just feel like maybe she isn't how you remembered her." "She always wanted to find paradise," you reply. "That wasn't all," he says, grimacing. [[What do you mean?->Port Pearl: What do you mean]]"She didn't just want paradise; she wanted to be rich. She had heard tell of a treasure in Port Pearl." "Martin said you went straight to Donalyn's Wall," you reply, confused. "Not quite," he says. "First we came here to Port Pearl, seeking the fabled golden statue. It's one of those mythical things, like the white and black tower that rises from the ocean, or the mystical Northman shaman, or the golden-scaled fish, or the elvish bride seeking her husband. "None of us wanted to go through with it. I mean, we didn't want to go to the Deadlands either, but she pushed us to consort with some seedy folks. I guess I should thank her, because that's how I fell into being a sailor. "Anyways, it got dangerous enough that I ducked out. Sami told me some more lurid details that I can't recall, but either way, I stayed here when something went belly up with their quest for the statue and they headed back to Donalyn's Wall." "Where is Sami?" you ask. "Don't know. And I'm happier not knowing. I like my life now. No need to dredge up the past." At that, he bids you farewell. [[Return to Port Pearl.->Port Pearl]]//''The Indifferent Suitor''// <div class="art art-springs"></div> (text-colour:orange)[This event is for the married hero. Here, "you" means them, even if it isn't their turn.] After a long day's worth of travel, you want nothing more than to sit down and relax your worn feet. You've heard of hot springs in the area, natural flowing waters that maintain their warm temperatures year-round. A bit of questioning from locals brings you to a bevy of pools laid out in a terrace-like structure, complete with a canopy of trees providing shade. "Wow, that looks like heaven," says Thistle wistfully. You couldn't agree more. As you approach, you're surprised to find that you're not the only party present at the springs. Indeed, there is a gaggle of young men and women, mostly humans, but a few half-elves as well. Your spouse turns to you, excitement in $spouseHer eyes. "I knew I made the right call by marrying you," (if: $spouseShe is "they")[they say](else:)[$spouseShe says]. Your glee is interrupted by a very distressed-looking young man. He wears a formal black suit and is sweating quite profusely. "Trader," he says, "thank God you've arrived. You are married, yes? Perhaps you can help settle a dispute. I've heard those of your profession are wise in many things beyond simply commerce." [[How can I help?->Suitor: How can I help]] [[I'm afraid we're just here to relax.->Suitor: Just here to relax]]"I'm afraid we're just here to relax," you say. The young man's shoulders slump. "Of course," he mutters, and he hurries off to find someone wiser. You sink into the hottest pool you can find and let the water draw the ache out of your feet and legs. Your spouse rests $spouseHer head on your shoulder, and before long, Thistle has fallen asleep sitting up in the water. Nobody makes any move to leave until the sun goes down. (text-colour:red)[Each hero heals half of their max WP.] [[End your turn.->Main]]"Do you see that woman over there?" he says, pointing to a woman sitting on a bench. She is marvelously done up, her hair shaped into an elaborate bun with crystalline latticework seemingly holding it in place. Pearls hang from her ears, and she wears a white dress of exquisite tailoring and a lilac overcoat with gold trim. "You don't see a woman as beautiful as that every day," Rudolph remarks. (if: $spouse is "Olwen")["I suppose I shall have to ignore that comment, Rudolph," Olwen says loftily, then winks at you. Rudolph hastens to apologize. He never knows how to act around the elf maiden. "Will you two stop nattering?" says the young man distractedly. "I have a real crisis on my hands." "Ah, yes, of course. Tell me, human, of your ails," says Olwen gravely.](else:)["Will you stop nattering?" says the young man distractedly. "I have a real crisis on my hands."] "Where to begin?" says the young man. "You may call me Ren. I am the steward for House Tywin." [[Continue.->Suitor: Ren's crisis]]"I figure you lot would know best, seeing as, well, at least one among you has successfully gone through with what we're attempting here. "The bride, Brylie of House Tywin, is set to be married to that little lord over there," he says, pointing to a young man in a blue surcoat standing off by himself by some trees. "But the infuriating sop of a person expresses no interest. Why, he refuses to even so much as look at Brylie. The survival of both our houses depends on this union. And by survival, I mean the livelihood of hundreds of hardworking men and women. It is critical that this occurs. What can be done?" [[Perhaps they're not in love.->Suitor: Not in love]] [[What does he say?->Suitor: The groom]] [[I don't think I can get involved in this.->Suitor: Decline]]"Of course they're not in love," replies Ren, sounding frustrated. "They just met." "Should a couple to be wed not love each other?" you ask. The man sighs. "Ideally," he says, "but love is not just plucked from the ether like an apple from a very tall man holding a lot of apples." "Or a tree," whispers Thistle sagely. "You know it can be created as well, bloomed, if there is but a seed, and I assure you there is a seed. I reckon, in fact, that most of love is in the tending, the little maintenances, rather than the sudden, inexplicable blush of instant attraction. Or wouldn't you agree?" (if: $spouse is "Olwen")["You are wise for a human," says Olwen. "But sometimes there is both. Also, you need to work on your metaphors a little bit." ][[What does he say?->Suitor: The groom]] [[I don't think I can get involved in this.->Suitor: Decline]]"He won't talk to me," says Ren, "but perhaps you can get words out of him." You head over to the young would-be groom standing by the tree. He regards you indifferently and says nothing. "How odd to be absent from your own wedding," you remark casually. "Is it my own wedding," he retorts, "or is it a process that I have no say in? More like my own imprisonment." (if: $spouse is "Olwen")["A little dramatic, don't you think?" says Olwen. ]"I'd choose your next words carefully," Rudolph whispers to you. "Say the wrong thing, and I suspect this lad will have no more words with us." [[Don't be ridiculous, boy. You're not being imprisoned. Sometimes you just need to man up and do what has to be done. In this case, that means marrying that girl.->Suitor: Man up]] [[You're right. Being forced into something you don't want is imprisonment. If I were you, I'd say goodbye to all this and hoof it before they can figure out that you've left.->Suitor: Hoof it]] [[Is it the prospect of marriage that doesn't sit well with you, or is it to whom you are going to be married that is the issue?->Suitor: Brylie]]"I'm sorry, but this is beyond my ability to counsel. I wish you good luck in your quest, Ren," you say. He sighs in defeat and waves you away. (text-colour:red)[Each hero heals half of their max WP.] [[End your turn.->Main]]His face goes cold. "Thank you for your counsel," he says, in a tone that makes it clear the counsel was not wanted, and he turns his back on you. Rudolph winces and gives you a look that says he warned you. Since he clearly has nothing more to say to you, you leave the two houses to their troubles and find a pool of your own. (text-colour:red)[Each hero heals half of their max WP.] [[End your turn.->Main]]He stares at you as if you had suggested he set fire to his own house. "And leave my family to answer for it? I think we're done here," he says, and he turns his back on you. Since he clearly has nothing more to say to you, you leave the two houses to their troubles and find a pool of your own. (text-colour:red)[Each hero heals half of their max WP.] [[End your turn.->Main]]"I said no more questions," he snaps, and he turns his back on you. Since he clearly has nothing more to say to you, you leave the two houses to their troubles and find a pool of your own. (text-colour:red)[Each hero heals half of their max WP.] [[End your turn.->Main]]"Spoken like someone with nothing to lose," he says, and he turns away from you. Since he clearly has nothing more to say to you, you leave the two houses to their troubles and find a pool of your own. (text-colour:red)[Each hero heals half of their max WP.] [[End your turn.->Main]]He nods as if he expected nothing else and goes back to staring at the trees. Since he clearly has nothing more to say to you, you leave the two houses to their troubles and find a pool of your own. (text-colour:red)[Each hero heals half of their max WP.] [[End your turn.->Main]]"What? No, there's nothing wrong with Brylie. She is more beautiful than I could have imagined, and she is kind, too. The way she twirls her hair..." He sighs wistfully, before abruptly scowling. "I'm not afraid of being married," he adds sourly. "I just don't think it's for me... in this particular situation. Don't ask me any more questions. I won't say more." [[But why not? If you like her, just get married.->Suitor: Why not]] [[All right, I won't ask you any more questions, but I will tell you that Ren is concerned about the livelihood of a lot of people. A lot hinges on this decision. You don't have to talk to me about it, but if you want to, I'd appreciate that.->Suitor: Two houses]]"Because Ren is only looking at half of the picture: he's looking at Tywin's finances. He doesn't realize the power dynamics. Yes, it's true, it will benefit our house, House Beljoie, as well. But Lord Tywin, Brylie's father, is a bit of a brute, and my father can sometimes be too amenable to the wishes of others. "I know that if we give Lord Tywin an inch, he will take a foot, and then several miles at least. No, however much I may wish for an arrangement," he says, glancing over at Brylie, "I must consider my duties as the future Lord Beljoie. Entering into this marriage would be bandaging up a bleeding leg wound only for the limb to be amputated later. As I said before, it is imprisonment, not only for me, but for my entire family." [[You seem very savvy in politics and in economics, but I can also see that you would actually really like to be married to this girl.->Suitor: You would]] [[You're being a pessimist and all doom and gloom. I say go for it and see what happens.->Suitor: Doom and gloom]]"Yes, I would," he says quietly. [[You know, I know a thing or two about business arrangements. They're all about leverage...->Suitor: Leverage]] [[Well, you're fresh out of luck, so I can't help you anymore. Sorry, I tried.->Suitor: Out of luck]]For the first time, the young lord turns to look at you properly. "Go on," he says. You sit down beside him under the trees and talk it through. Lord Tywin wants his alliance, but House Beljoie needs protection from a father-in-law who takes miles where he is given inches, and the answer the two of you settle on is a third party bound to neither house: you. As a Trader, you will hold the dowry and witness the terms, and any clause that touches Beljoie's lands, tolls or levies will need the seals of both houses as well as yours. That way, Lord Tywin still gets his alliance, and the young lord can marry Brylie without putting his family at risk. He reads over the new terms several times before he agrees to them, looking happier than he has all day. Ren signs it, relieved to get the process over with, and thanks you. Later, you see Lord Tywin furiously yelling at Ren before throwing up his hands in defeat. Before you leave the springs, a grey-haired man with the young lord's chin finds you and clasps your hand in both of his. "I am Lord Beljoie," he says. "My son tells me our house owes you a great deal, Trader, and House Beljoie does not forget its friends." (set: $supported to true, $beljoie to true) (text-colour:orange)[Your party is now Supported: House Beljoie pledges its support.] (text-colour:orange)[House Beljoie Support: at the start of every fight, each hero gains 6 DEF.] [[End your turn.->Main]]//''Traveler's Rest''// The woman’s brow furrows. “I remember the girl. To live at Traveler’s Rest requires a certain sacrifice: it is a very simple life, and often not exciting enough for our young people. Marla is looking for paradise, and though we ourselves feel very blessed and content, I suppose she was expecting something more. “She said also that a great foe was chasing her, and that she must find a weapon to slay this foe. You must seek answers in the caves nearby.” (text-colour:lime)[Travel to the nearby spot marked ''E'' on the map to find out what happened to Marla.] [[Back->Traveler's Rest]]//''The Valley of Graves''// <div class="art art-elite"></div> You find your way to the caves that the woman at Traveler’s Rest told you about. Ascending the mountainside, you pass through a cave whose entrance opens like a maw with fangs. When you pass through it, you come out into a hidden valley nestled within the mountains, and see rows and rows of graves, as far and deep as the eye can see. A lone figure is shoveling dirt into an unmarked grave. He turns to you. He is dressed in a fine purple suit and a purple top hat, and he wears a monocle. “Welcome to my valley. I am Gravedigger Kairos,” he says. “What happened?” you ask. “What have you done with Marla?” He laughs, a low, throaty chuckle. “What have I done to her?” he says. Then he gestures to another wordless headstone. “That is for you,” he says, “for daring to speak my master’s name.” (text-colour:purple)[Fight Gravedigger Kairos. Take out his boss card.] (if: $heroes is 4)[(text-colour:purple)[Four heroes: also draw 2 enemies from the Deadlands enemy deck. They fight beside him, act after him in the order drawn, and pay their printed drops.] ](if: $wolfPack is true)[(text-colour:purple)[Your wolf pack: in the first round, one enemy of your choice becomes Vulnerable 1.] ](if: $beljoie is true)[(text-colour:purple)[House Beljoie’s men-at-arms: each hero starts this fight with 6 DEF.] ] [[We won.->Gravedigger Kairos: Victory]] (link: "Every hero fell.")[(set: $lostTo to "kairos")(go-to: "Run lost")]//''Victory''// The man fights with a feeling of inevitability, his movements slow and calculated, but his blows crushing. It seems as though your blows do almost nothing to him, but at last he falls. You breathe a sigh of relief. He totters off and collapses into the open grave he had dug for you. In his hands, you find a scrap of paper with the word “Marla” on it, and then “Sunken City.” (text-colour:green)[Congratulations, you have beaten Scenario 1. Move on to Scenario 2.] (link: "Start a new run")[(restart:)]
